definition_zh: 下级的；从属的；次要的；下属；部下；使服从；使处于次要地位
definition_en: lower in rank or importance, a person who works under another, or to put someone or something in a less important position
core_image: 一排人依次往下站队，下一个人站在上一个人的后下方
scene: 公司年会上，部门经理把年度计划交待给手下的几位主管。At the annual meeting the director handed the plan down to her subordinates in the branches.
sceneCN: 这里 subordinate 是「下属、部下」（第 4 个义项：在层级中位于别人之下的人）；句意：年会上，主管把年度计划交给各分部的下属。

pos.zh: 使服从；使处于次要地位

collocations.zh: 把某事物置于次要地位

derivatives.zh: 由 subordinate 加 -ion 构成，义为「从属；服从；次要地位」
由 subordinate 加 -ive 构成，义为「表示从属的」，多用于语法术语
由否定前缀 in- 加 subordinate 构成，义为「不服从的；违抗上级的」
subordinate 的现在分词用作形容词，义为「引导从句的」，如从属连词

senses.title: Lower in rank
senses.definition: having a lower rank or position than someone else in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 在组织中的级别或职位低于别人
senses.example: A subordinate officer reported the delay to the captain.
senses.exampleCN: 一名下级军官向舰长报告了延误。
senses.why: Latin sub- means under, and ordinare means to arrange, so a subordinate item is arranged under another in the order of rank.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sub- 表示「在下」，ordinare 表示「排列」，所以从属者就是在等级序列里被排在下面的人。

senses.title: Dependent on something
senses.definition: controlled by or dependent on something more important or powerful
senses.definitionCN: 受更重要或更有力的事物控制或支配
senses.example: In this system, local courts are subordinate to the high court.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个体系里，地方法院隶属于高等法院。
senses.why: The order on the page becomes an order of power: whatever stands under another in the arrangement must also obey it.
senses.whyCN: 纸面上的「排在下」变成权力上的「管在下」：排列中在下面的一方，也得听命于上面一方。

senses.title: Less important
senses.definition: treated as less important than something else
senses.definitionCN: 被视为不如另一事物重要
senses.example: He let personal ambition stay subordinate to the team goal.
senses.exampleCN: 他让个人野心服从于团队目标。
senses.why: Under in rank also means under in worth, so anything placed below the main concern counts as subordinate.
senses.whyCN: 在等级上「在下」也延伸为分量上「在下」，凡是放在主要关注点之下的事物都算次要。

senses.title: A person lower in rank
senses.definition: a person who works under the authority of another
senses.definitionCN: 在他人管辖之下工作的人
senses.example: The manager treats every subordinate with the same respect.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理对每一位下属都同样尊重。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the person who occupies the lower place in the line.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接名词化，就是指在队伍里占据较低位置的那个人。

senses.title: A grammatically dependent clause
senses.definition: a clause that depends on a main clause and cannot stand alone
senses.definitionCN: 依附于主句、不能单独成句的分句
senses.example: The subordinate clause begins with a word like although.
senses.exampleCN: 这个从句以 although 之类的词开头。
senses.why: Grammar reuses the image in the sentence itself, where one clause is arranged under another and cannot stand alone.
senses.whyCN: 语法把这幅画面搬进句子内部：一个分句被排在另一个分句之下，不能独立成立。

senses.title: To make less important
senses.titleCN: 使处于次要地位；把……降格
senses.definition: to treat something as less important than something else
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物视为不如另一事物重要
senses.example: The report subordinates cost to safety at every stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告在每个阶段都把成本置于安全之下。
senses.why: The verb action is to move something down the arrangement and keep it there.
senses.whyCN: 动词的意思就是把某物在序列中往下挪，并让它一直待在那个位置。

senses.title: To bring under control
senses.definition: to place someone or something under the control of another
senses.definitionCN: 把人或事物置于他人的控制之下
senses.example: The new law subordinates private contracts to public rules.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律让私人合同服从公共规则。
senses.why: Putting a thing under an authority is the action side of being subordinate to that authority.
senses.whyCN: 把事物置于某权威之下，正是「隶属于该权威」这层关系的动作面。

intro.en: Subordinate goes back to Latin sub-, under, plus ordinare, to arrange or set in order, through the medieval Latin adjective subordinatus.
intro.cn: subordinate 源自拉丁语 sub-（在下）加 ordinare（排列、整理），经中世纪拉丁语的形容词 subordinatus 进入英语。

items.en: Ordo means a row or order, and ordinare means to arrange in that order.
items.cn: ordo 意为行列、次序，ordinare 意为按这个次序排列。

items.en: The prefix sub- means under or below, as in many Latin compounds.
items.cn: 前缀 sub- 意为在下、低于，常见于大量拉丁语复合词。

items.en: Subordinatus means placed under another in rank or authority.
items.cn: subordinatus 意为在等级或权力上被置于他人之下。

items.en: Subordinate enters English as an adjective used in church and legal ordering.
items.cn: subordinate 作为形容词进入英语，多用于教会与法律的等级安排。

items.en: The noun for a person of lower rank and the verb meaning to bring under control appear.
items.cn: 表示「下属」的名词与表示「使服从」的动词先后出现。

items.en: Grammarians use it for dependent clauses, and management writers for office hierarchy.
items.cn: 语法学家用它指从属分句，管理学著作用它指职场的层级关系。

note.en: Subordinate sits in the order family of Latin ordinare, close to its own derivatives, and in meaning it stands between inferior, junior, and secondary.
note.cn: subordinate 属于拉丁语 ordinare 的「次序」词族，与其自身的派生词相邻；在意义上则与 inferior、junior、secondary 相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being lower in rank or under control
entries.definitionCN: 从属；服从；处于次要地位的状态

entries.definition: to order or appoint, sharing the Latin root of arranging in order
entries.definitionCN: 规定；委任，与 subordinate 共享「按次序排列」的拉丁词根

entries.definition: an arrangement or sequence, from Latin ordo
entries.definitionCN: 次序；顺序，出自拉丁语 ordo

entries.definition: lower in rank or quality
entries.definitionCN: 级别或质量较低的，常带贬义，subordinate 则较为中性

entries.definition: younger or of lower position
entries.definitionCN: 较年轻的；职位较低的

entries.definition: of less importance than something else
entries.definitionCN: 次要的；第二位的

normalIntro.en: Subordinate is built from sub-, under, and ordinare, to arrange, so the whole word pictures someone arranged under someone else.
normalIntro.cn: subordinate 由 sub-（在下）加 ordinare（排列）构成，整个词画出的就是「被排在某人下面」的人。

normal.en: Latin sub- means under, as in submarine and subway.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 表示在下，submarine、subway 都用同一个前缀。

normal.en: Ordinare means to arrange in order, the source of order and ordain.
normal.cn: ordinare 意为按次序排列，order 与 ordain 都出自它。

normal.en: A subordinate clause is a clause arranged under a main clause.
normal.cn: subordinate clause 就是排在主句之下的分句，即从句。

normal.en: The adjective ends in a weak -ate, but the verb ends in a clear -ate.
normal.cn: 形容词词尾 -ate 读得轻而弱，动词词尾 -ate 读得清楚而重。

normal.en: Insubordinate adds in- and means refusing to stay under authority.
normal.cn: insubordinate 加上否定前缀 in-，意为不愿待在权威之下的「不服从的」。

abstract.en: Picture name tags hanging one below another on a staircase.
abstract.cn: 想象一串名牌挂在楼梯扶手上，一个比一个低。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a card down under a heavier card.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一张卡片按到另一张更重的卡片下面。

abstract.en: Picture a small weight kept under the main weight, then moved there deliberately.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小砝码被放到大砝码之下，并且是特意摆过去的。

examples.en: The project was subordinate to the larger plan for the city.
examples.cn: 这个项目隶属于城市整体规划之下。

examples.en: Good managers listen to their subordinates before deciding.
examples.cn: 好的管理者会在做决定前听取下属意见。

examples.en: Some economists subordinate growth to stability.
examples.cn: 一些经济学家让增长服从于稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「下属的」——subordinate 听起来像「下属的」，正是排在你下面的人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ ordinare（排列、整理，源于 ordo「行列、次序」）→ 中世纪拉丁语 subordinatus（被排在下面的）→ 英语 subordinate，核心义「在次序中排在他人之下」，故有「下级的」「从属的」「次要的」「下属」与「使服从」诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Subordinate starts as a rank adjective, widens to dependence and lesser importance, turns into the person below, borrows a grammatical sense, and ends with the verbs of demoting and controlling.
sensesIntro.cn: subordinate 先作形容词表示级别较低，扩展到从属与次要，再名词化为「下属」，又借入语法表示从句，最后派生出「使处于次要地位」与「使服从」两个动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: people standing in a line of rank, each one placed under the one above.
core.cn: 核心意象：人们按等级站成一列，每一个都排在上一级之下。

branches.en: Lower rank is the literal sense of the arranged line.
branches.cn: 级别较低是这条等级线最字面的意思。

branches.en: From position to power: the lower one depends on the higher.
branches.cn: 从位置转到权力：排在下的一方依赖排在上的一方。

branches.en: Less importance is the same image applied to value.
branches.cn: 次要地位是同一画面在价值上的投射。

branches.en: The person in the lower place becomes the noun subordinate.
branches.cn: 站在较低位置的那个人，名词化就是 subordinate。

branches.en: Grammar and the two verbs extend the line into clauses and into action.
branches.cn: 语法义与两个动词义分别把这条线延伸到分句与动作之中。

intro.en: Subordinate pairs the Latin prefix sub- with the root ordinare, in the same family as order, ordain, and ordinal, and it gains -ion, -ive, and in- in its derivatives.
intro.cn: subordinate 用拉丁语前缀 sub- 与词根 ordinare 拼成，与 order、ordain、ordinal 同属一族；派生词再带上 -ion、-ive 与否定前缀 in-。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- means under, ordo means a row or order, and ordinare means to arrange in order.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 意为在下，ordo 意为行列、次序，ordinare 意为按次序排列。

items.example: The prefix sub- places the word below another.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把这个词放在另一个词之下。

items.example: Ordo supplies the idea of a rank order.
items.exampleCN: ordo 提供「等级次序」的观念。

items.example: Ordinare is the root shared with order.
items.exampleCN: ordinare 是与 order 共享的词根。

items.example: Subordinatus is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: subordinatus 是这个英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Order comes from the same Latin ordo.
items.exampleCN: order 出自同一个拉丁语 ordo。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms subordination.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 subordination。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms subordinative.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 subordinative。

items.example: The prefix in- forms insubordinate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 insubordinate。

items.example: The ending -ate marks the adjective and verb forms alike.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 同时标志形容词形式与动词形式。

items.example: The adjective keeps the arranged-order image.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留了「排列次序」的画面。

latinEntries.meaning: to arrange, to set in order

definition_zh: 订阅；付费订购；定期订阅；赞同；同意；签名；捐款；认购
definition_en: to pay regularly to receive a service or publication, to agree with an idea, or to write ones name at the bottom of a document
core_image: 在文件末尾一笔一画签下自己的名字，表示认下这件事
scene: 月底手机弹出提醒，说会员服务即将到期，问是否继续付费。A reminder on my phone asks whether I want to subscribe for another year of the online library.
sceneCN: 这里 subscribe 是「付费订阅」（第 1 个义项：定期付钱以持续获得某项服务）；句意：手机提醒问我是否要再订阅一年在线图书馆。

pos.zh: 订阅；付费订购（报刊、服务）
签署（文件）；捐款；认购（股份）

collocations.zh: 订阅（报刊、频道）；赞同（观点）

derivatives.zh: 由 subscribe 加 -er 构成，义为「订阅者；订户；用户」，也指「认捐人」
由 subscribe 加 -tion 构成，义为「订阅；订阅费；认购」
由 over- 加 subscribe 构成，义为「认购超额；超额订购」，股票发行常用
由否定前缀 un- 加 subscribe 构成，义为「取消订阅」，多用于邮件与推送

senses.title: To pay for regular access
senses.definition: to pay regularly to receive a magazine, service, or online content
senses.definitionCN: 定期付费以获得杂志、服务或网络内容
senses.example: She subscribes to three science magazines.
senses.exampleCN: 她订阅了三份科普杂志。
senses.why: Latin sub- means under and scribere means to write, and the first subscribers put their names under a promise to pay for a series of issues.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sub- 表示「在下」，scribere 表示「写」；最早的订户是在承诺支付的文书下面写下自己的名字，于是「签名认下」变成「订阅」。

senses.title: To agree with an idea
senses.definition: to agree with an opinion, theory, or course of action
senses.definitionCN: 赞同某种看法、理论或做法
senses.example: Not every economist subscribes to that theory.
senses.exampleCN: 并非每位经济学家都赞同那个理论。
senses.why: To sign under a statement is to put your name to it, and putting your name to a view is exactly agreeing with it.
senses.whyCN: 在一段说法下面签名，就是把自己的名字押上去，而把名字押上一种看法，正是赞同它。

senses.title: To write ones name under a document
senses.definition: to sign a document as a formal act of commitment
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上正式签名以示承诺
senses.example: Both parties subscribed the contract before the notary.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在公证人面前签署了合同。
senses.why: This is the literal old sense: the pen moves along the dotted line under the text.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的古老义：笔沿着文字下面的签名线一路写下去。

senses.title: To promise money
senses.definition: to promise to give money to a cause or fund
senses.definitionCN: 承诺为某项事业或基金捐款
senses.example: Residents subscribed generously to the new hospital fund.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们为新医院基金慷慨认捐。
senses.why: A signed pledge was a written promise of money, so signing under a list grew into the act of donating.
senses.whyCN: 签名的认捐书就是一份书面的给钱承诺，于是「在名单下签名」长成了「捐款」。

senses.title: To buy new shares
senses.definition: to apply and pay for new shares or securities when they are offered
senses.definitionCN: 在发行时申请并付款购买新股或证券
senses.example: Investors subscribed for the full amount within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者在一小时内就足额认购了。
senses.why: Finance keeps the promise sense: the investor writes a name on the offer sheet and binds himself to pay.
senses.whyCN: 金融沿用「承诺」这一层：投资者在发行单上写下名字，就等于约束自己付款。

senses.title: To support a cause
senses.definition: to give support, often money, to a publication or public project
senses.definitionCN: 为出版物或公共项目提供支持，常指出钱
senses.example: Several local firms subscribed to the rebuilding of the library.
senses.exampleCN: 几家本地企业出资支持图书馆的重建。
senses.why: Support shown by writing a name under a list of backers is a softer version of donating.
senses.whyCN: 在赞助名单下写下名字所示的支援，是捐款义更轻缓的一种延伸。

intro.en: Subscribe comes from Latin subscribere, to write underneath, built from sub-, under, and scribere, to write.
intro.cn: subscribe 来自拉丁语 subscribere（写在下面），由 sub-（在下）与 scribere（写）构成。

items.en: Scribere means to write, and gives script, scribe, and describe.
items.cn: scribere 意为书写，script、scribe、describe 都出自它。

items.en: Subscribere means to write underneath a document, especially as a signature or endorsement.
items.cn: subscribere 意为在文书下面书写，尤指签名或背书。

items.en: The participle subscriptsus is also used for a person who signs as witness or as a supporter.
items.cn: 分词形式也用来指签名作证或表示支持的人。

items.en: Subscribe enters English meaning to sign at the foot of a document.
items.cn: subscribe 进入英语时意为在文件末尾签名。

items.en: Booksellers sell copies in advance to people whose names are written in a list, so subscribing becomes ordering a publication.
items.cn: 书商预先向名单上的人售书，于是 subscribe 转指订购出版物。

items.en: Digital services make the word mean paying regularly for online access.
items.cn: 数字服务让这个词转而表示定期付费以持续使用线上服务。

note.en: Subscribe belongs to the Latin writing family of scribere, and in meaning it stands beside renew, pledge, and its old spelling rival, ascribe.
note.cn: subscribe 属于拉丁语 scribere（书写）词族；在意义上与 renew、pledge 相邻，也常与拼写相近的 ascribe 混淆。

entries.definition: the act of subscribing, or the fee paid for it
entries.definitionCN: 订阅行为或订阅费用

entries.definition: a person who subscribes
entries.definitionCN: 订阅者；订户

entries.definition: to say that something is caused by a particular person or thing
entries.definitionCN: 把……归因于；只是拼写相近且共享词根 scribere，前缀不同，词源路径有别

entries.definition: to continue a subscription for a further period
entries.definitionCN: 为订阅续期，subscribe 指第一次订阅

entries.definition: a serious promise, often of money
entries.definitionCN: 正式承诺，常指认捐钱款

entries.definition: to sign the back of a document or publicly support something
entries.definitionCN: 在文件背面签名；公开支持某事物

normalIntro.en: Subscribe is literally to write under: the name goes at the foot of the page, and every later sense grows out of that signature.
normalIntro.cn: subscribe 字面意思就是「在下面写」：名字落在页面底部，后来各种意义都从这一笔签名长出来。

normal.en: Latin sub- means under and scribere means to write.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 表示在下，scribere 表示书写。

normal.en: Scribe, script, and describe all share the root scribere.
normal.cn: scribe、script、describe 都共享词根 scribere。

normal.en: Subscribe to a channel means putting your name under its list.
normal.cn: subscribe to a channel 就是在频道名单下写上自己的名字。

normal.en: Unsubscribe adds un- and means to take your name off that list.
normal.cn: unsubscribe 加否定前缀 un-，意为把名字从名单上撤下。

normal.en: Compare ascribe: it uses ad- and puts the blame or credit onto a cause.
normal.cn: 对比 ascribe：它用前缀 ad-，把功劳或责任「推给」某个原因。

abstract.en: Picture a pen moving along the dotted line at the bottom of a form.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔沿着表格底部的虚线一路写下去。

abstract.en: Picture a name added to a long list of readers on a shop notice board.
abstract.cn: 想象书店告示板上那一长串读者名单里，又添上一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a name written at the head of an empty page that is still being filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一页还没写满的纸，顶上先写好了名字，往下随时可以补内容。

examples.en: You need to subscribe before you can read the full article.
examples.cn: 你需要先订阅才能阅读全文。

examples.en: Few researchers subscribe to the idea that the letter was forged.
examples.cn: 很少有研究者赞同这封信是伪造的说法。

examples.en: The magazine has gained ten thousand new subscribers this year.
examples.cn: 这家杂志今年新增了一万名订户。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「塞不实在」——订阅前先想想，别把订费花得不明不白；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ scribere（书写）→ subscribere（在文书下面书写、签名）→ 英语 subscribe，核心义「在下面签名认下这件事」，故有「签署」「赞同」「认购」「捐款」「订阅」诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Subscribe begins with paid regular access, widens to agreement, returns to the literal signature, then moves into donating, buying shares, and supporting a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: subscribe 先指定期付费订阅，扩展到赞同，再回到字面的签名义，随后延伸到捐款、认购股份与赞助事业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name written under a text, binding the writer to what stands above.
core.cn: 核心意象：在文字下面写下名字，让自己与上面的内容绑定。

branches.en: Paid regular access is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 定期付费订阅是今天最主要的义项。

branches.en: Agreement is the signature added under a statement.
branches.cn: 赞同就是在某种说法下面补上自己的签名。

branches.en: The literal signature keeps the earliest meaning alive.
branches.cn: 字面的签名义保留着最古老的意思。

branches.en: Donating and sponsoring are money promises written on a list of helpers.
branches.cn: 捐款与赞助都是写在一份支援名单上的出钱承诺。

branches.en: Buying shares is the same promise made on a financial offer sheet.
branches.cn: 认购股份只是把同样的承诺写在金融发行单上。

intro.en: Subscribe joins the Latin prefix sub- to the root scribere, the same writing root as script and describe, and its family adds -er, -tion, over-, and un-.
intro.cn: subscribe 用拉丁语前缀 sub- 接住词根 scribere，与 script、describe 共享同一个「书写」词根；词族再带出 -er、-tion、over- 与 un-。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- means under, and scribere means to write, so subscribere means to write underneath.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 意为在下，scribere 意为书写，因此 subscribere 意为写在下面。

items.example: The prefix sub- puts the writing below the text.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把书写的位置放在正文之下。

items.example: Scribere is the writing root shared with script.
items.exampleCN: scribere 是与 script 共享的「书写」词根。

items.example: Subscribere is the direct ancestor of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: subscribere 是这个英语动词的直接祖先。

items.example: Scriptum gives script and subscription their written core.
items.exampleCN: scriptum 给 script 与 subscription 提供了「文字」的核心。

items.meaning: to write down the features of something
items.example: Describe combines de- with the same root scribere.
items.exampleCN: describe 把 de- 与同一个词根 scribere 结合。

items.example: The suffix -er forms subscriber.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 subscriber。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms subscription.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 构成 subscription。

items.example: The prefix over- forms oversubscribe.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 构成 oversubscribe。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unsubscribe.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unsubscribe。

items.example: The root -scribe links subscribe with describe and prescribe.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -scribe 把 subscribe 与 describe、prescribe 连在一起。

definition_zh: 订阅；订阅费；签名；批准；捐款；认购
definition_en: an arrangement or fee for receiving a service regularly, the act of signing a document, or money given to support a cause
core_image: 一叠写满名字的名单，每个名字下面都记着一笔应付的钱
scene: 家里的书房里，父亲把几家报纸的订阅单收进一个信封，按月付款。My father keeps the subscription notices for three newspapers in one envelope and pays for them monthly.
sceneCN: 这里 subscription 是「订阅」（第 1 个义项：定期付费以持续获得报刊或服务）；句意：父亲把三份报纸的订阅通知收在同一个信封里，按月付钱。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词词尾 -tion 所得的动词原形，义为「订阅；赞同；签署」
由 subscribe 加 -er 构成，义为「订户；订阅者」
与 subscription 同出 subscriptus（写在下方的），义为「下标」，也指「下角标符号」
由 subscription 加 -less 构成，义为「无需订阅的」

senses.title: A paid arrangement for regular service
senses.definition: an arrangement in which you pay regularly to receive a magazine, service, or online content
senses.definitionCN: 定期付费以持续获得杂志、服务或网络内容的安排
senses.example: My subscription to the library database runs for twelve months.
senses.exampleCN: 我的图书馆数据库订阅有效期为十二个月。
senses.why: Latin subscriptio is a writing underneath, and the noun first named a signed order, which grew into the standing arrangement behind it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 subscriptio 意为「写在下方」，名词最早指签了名的订单，后来转指订单背后的那份长期安排。

senses.title: The money paid for it
senses.definition: the sum of money paid for such an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 为上述订阅安排支付的费用
senses.example: The yearly subscription costs less than two coffees a month.
senses.exampleCN: 每年订阅费还不如每月两杯咖啡贵。
senses.why: The signed promise was a promise of money, so the noun also names the amount owed.
senses.whyCN: 签了字的承诺本质上是一份给钱的承诺，所以名词也指应付的那笔款项。

senses.title: The act of signing
senses.definition: the act of writing ones name at the foot of a document to show agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在文件末尾写下名字以示同意的行为
senses.example: The treaty required subscription by both ministers.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约需要两位部长签署。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal meaning, kept in formal and historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最字面的意思，多保留在正式与历史文献中。

senses.title: Formal approval in the margin
senses.definition: formal agreement or approval, shown by writing a name under a text
senses.definitionCN: 通过署名表示正式同意或批准
senses.example: The articles of the church were drawn up by subscription.
senses.exampleCN: 该教会的章程是经会众签名认可后制定的。
senses.why: When names are collected under a statement, the signature becomes a vote of assent.
senses.whyCN: 当名字被收集在某段文字下面时，签名就变成了一张赞同票。

senses.title: A gift of money to a cause
senses.definition: money promised or given to support a charity, fund, or building
senses.definitionCN: 为资助慈善、基金或建筑工程而承诺或付出的钱
senses.example: Donors collected a large subscription for the new school roof.
senses.exampleCN: 捐赠者为新校舍屋顶募集了一大笔捐款。
senses.why: A list of names with sums beside them is how towns and churches once raised money, and the whole list became a subscription.
senses.whyCN: 在名字旁记下金额，是旧时城镇与教会募款的方法，整份名单合起来就叫一个 subscription。

senses.title: Commitment to buy new shares
senses.definition: a formal commitment to buy new shares or securities being offered
senses.definitionCN: 对正在发行的新股或证券作出的正式购买承诺
senses.example: The subscription for the new shares closed on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 新股的认购在上周五截止。
senses.why: Finance repeats the pattern: the investor signs an order sheet, and the signed commitment is itself called the subscription.
senses.whyCN: 金融领域重复着同一模式：投资者签到一张订单上，这份签了字的承诺本身就被称为 subscription。

intro.en: Subscription comes from Latin subscriptio, a writing at the foot of a document, from the verb subscribere, to write underneath.
intro.cn: subscription 来自拉丁语 subscriptio（写在文书末尾的东西），源自动词 subscribere（写在下面）。

items.en: Scribere means to write, and subscriptio means a writing added underneath.
items.cn: scribere 意为书写，subscriptio 意为在下面附加的书写。

items.en: In Rome a subscriptio could be the signature, the footnote, or the answer written under a legal petition.
items.cn: 在罗马，subscriptio 既可指签名，也可指附注，还可指写在法律请愿书下面的答复。

items.en: Late Latin subscriptio also means an attestation or an endorsement of a document.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，subscriptio 也指对文书的见证或背书。

items.en: Subscription enters English as the act of signing, and of subscribing money to a cause.
items.cn: subscription 进入英语时指签名，也指为某项事业出资。

items.en: The publishing trade names the paid order for a series of books a subscription.
items.cn: 出版业把对成套图书的付费订购称作 subscription。

items.en: With digital media the word settles into its main sense of regular paid access.
items.cn: 进入数字媒体时代，这个词稳定在「定期付费使用」这一主要义上。

note.en: Subscription belongs to the Latin writing family of scribere, and in meaning it sits between membership, enrollment, and dues.
note.cn: subscription 属于拉丁语 scribere（书写）词族；在意义上位于 membership、enrollment、dues 之间。

entries.definition: to pay regularly for a service or to sign a document
entries.definitionCN: 订阅或签署，是 subscription 的动词原形

entries.definition: a small character written below the line
entries.definitionCN: 下标；写在基线下方的小字符

entries.definition: a written order for medicine
entries.definitionCN: 处方；只是前缀 pre- 与 sub- 不同，共享写词根 scribere

entries.definition: the state of belonging to a group, often with a fee
entries.definitionCN: 会员身份，常伴有会费

entries.definition: the act of joining a course or organization officially
entries.definitionCN: 注册；报名加入

entries.definition: money that is paid regularly to belong to a club or union
entries.definitionCN: 定期缴纳的会费

normalIntro.en: Subscription keeps the written underside of subscribe: every subscription began as a name and a sum written under a heading.
normalIntro.cn: subscription 保留着 subscribe 的「写在下面」：每一份订阅最初都只是标题下方的一个名字和一笔金额。

normal.en: Sub- is under, and scribere is to write, so subscription is a writing underneath.
normal.cn: sub- 表示在下，scribere 表示书写，所以 subscription 就是写在下面的文字。

normal.en: A subscription fee is the money under the name.
normal.cn: subscription fee 就是名字下面那笔钱。

normal.en: The suffix -tion turns the verb subscribe into the act and its result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -tion 把动词 subscribe 变成行为及其结果。

normal.en: Cancel a subscription means taking that name off the list again.
normal.cn: cancel a subscription 就是再把那个名字从名单上撤掉。

normal.en: Compare prescription: same written root, but pre- means before, as in writing beforehand.
normal.cn: 对比 prescription：同样出自书写词根，只是 pre- 表示在前，即预先写下。

abstract.en: Picture a list of names with tiny sums pencilled beside each one.
abstract.cn: 想象一份名单，每个名字旁都用铅笔写着一小笔金额。

abstract.en: Picture a signed order card sliding into a drawer that fills up month by month.
abstract.cn: 想象一张签过字的订购卡滑进抽屉，抽屉一月一月地越攒越满。

abstract.en: Picture a name written at the head of a list that is still being added to by others.
abstract.cn: 想象一份名单顶上的名字刚写好，后面还不断有人在往下添。

examples.en: The subscription renews automatically unless you cancel it.
examples.cn: 除非你取消，订阅会自动续期。

examples.en: Many readers moved their subscriptions from paper to digital.
examples.cn: 许多读者把订阅从纸本转到了电子版。

examples.en: The share issue raised a record subscription within two days.
examples.cn: 这次股票发行在两天内创下了认购纪录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「替科斯普理逊」——替订户把刊物送到手里，就是「订阅」服务；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ scribere（书写）→ subscriptio（写在文书末尾的文字、签名、附署）→ 英语 subscription，核心义「写在下面并认下的东西」，故有「签名」「批准」「捐款」「认购」与「订阅」诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Subscription starts with paid regular service, names the money paid, recovers the literal signature and its approval force, then widens to donations and to share commitments.
sensesIntro.cn: subscription 先指定期付费订阅，接着指所付的钱，再回到字面的签名及其批准效力，随后扩展到捐款与股份认购。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a list of names with sums written underneath each one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份名单，每个名字下面都记着一笔钱。

branches.en: Regular paid service is the sense people meet every day.
branches.cn: 定期付费服务是日常最常遇到的义项。

branches.en: The fee names the sum that stood under the name.
branches.cn: 订阅费就是名字下面那一笔金额。

branches.en: Signing and approval keep the oldest legal meaning.
branches.cn: 签名与批准保留着最古老的法律含义。

branches.en: Donation is the list of names turned into a fund.
branches.cn: 捐款就是那份名单变成的募款。

branches.en: Share subscription moves the same signed promise into the market.
branches.cn: 股份认购把同样的签名承诺搬进了市场。

intro.en: Subscription pairs the prefix sub- with the Latin writing root scribere, through the noun ending -tion, and links to subscribe, subscriber, and subscript.
intro.cn: subscription 通过名词词尾 -tion，把前缀 sub- 与拉丁语书写词根 scribere 拼在一起，并与 subscribe、subscriber、subscript 相连。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- means under, scribere means to write, and subscriptio means a writing underneath or a signature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 意为在下，scribere 意为书写，subscriptio 意为写在下面的文字或签名。

items.example: The prefix sub- marks the position under the text.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 标明文字下方的位置。

items.example: Scribere is the writing root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: scribere 是整族词的书写词根。

items.example: Subscriptio is the direct Latin source of the word.
items.exampleCN: subscriptio 是这个英语词的直接拉丁来源。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms subscription from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 把动词变成 subscription。

items.example: The root -script- appears in manuscript and transcript.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -script- 出现在 manuscript 与 transcript 中。

items.example: The suffix -er forms subscriber.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 subscriber。

items.example: The suffix -less forms subscriptionless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 subscriptionless。

items.example: The prefix pre- forms prescription in the same family.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 在同族词中构成 prescription。

items.example: Subscriber names one member of the family.
items.exampleCN: subscriber 指这一词族中的一环。

definition_zh: 补贴；资助；给…发放补助金
definition_en: to pay part of the cost of something so that it can be offered more cheaply
core_image: 一只手把一袋钱塞到柜台下面，替顾客垫上一部分账单
scene: 政府想让孩子都能喝上牛奶，于是掏钱替学校垫上一部分账单。The government agreed to subsidise milk for every primary school child.
sceneCN: 这里 subsidise 是「补贴、资助」（第 1 个义项：出钱替别人分担一部分费用）；句意：政府同意为每个小学生喝的牛奶提供补贴。

pos.zh: 补贴；资助；给…发放补助金

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 subsidium（后备援助）经英语化而来，指政府发放的补贴、补助金
由 subsidise 加 -ed 构成，指享受补贴的、受资助的
由 subsidise 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，指补贴行为或补贴本身
同源于 subsidiary，本义「后备的、辅助的」，引申为附属的；作名词指子公司
由 subsidiary 加 -ity 构成，指辅助原则，即上级只在必要时介入

senses.title: To pay part of a cost
senses.definition: to pay part of the cost of a service or product so that buyers pay less
senses.definitionCN: 替某项服务或产品付掉一部分成本，使购买者少花钱
senses.example: The city subsidises bus fares for students.
senses.exampleCN: 该市为学生的公交票价提供补贴。
senses.why: The Latin subsidium was a reserve force kept behind the front line, so subsidising is money kept in reserve to help a weaker side.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 subsidium 原指留在战线后方待命的后备部队，补贴就是留一笔钱在背后支援较弱的一方。

senses.title: To support an activity with money
senses.definition: to give money to an organisation or activity so that it can keep going
senses.definitionCN: 给某个组织或活动提供资金，使它能够继续运转
senses.example: The council subsidises the theatre so tickets stay cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 市政委员会资助剧院，好让票价保持低廉。
senses.why: A subsidy is help from outside, so the verb also covers keeping a struggling venture alive with money.
senses.whyCN: 补贴本身就是来自外部的援助，所以这个动词也指用钱让一个艰难维持的事业活下去。

senses.title: To enable by paying
senses.titleCN: 以补贴方式使负担得起
senses.definition: to make something affordable for people by covering part of the price
senses.definitionCN: 替人们付掉一部分价格，使某物变得负担得起
senses.example: The scheme subsidises childcare for low-income families.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划为低收入家庭补贴托儿费用。
senses.why: The purpose of a reserve force is to save the exhausted troops, so the modern verb focuses on the person who is relieved of part of the bill.
senses.whyCN: 后备部队的作用是解救筋疲力尽的主力，因此现代用法把重点放在被减去一部分账单的人身上。

senses.title: To buy allegiance with money
senses.definition: to pay someone or a group to support a cause
senses.definitionCN: 给某人或某个团体钱，以换取他们支持某项事业
senses.example: Critics say the subsidies simply buy votes.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说这些补贴只是在收买选票。
senses.why: The same notion of paying for support can turn into payment for loyalty, which is why the verb has a suspicious use.
senses.whyCN: 「花钱换取支持」这一观念可以转为「花钱换忠诚」，所以这个词也有带怀疑色彩的用法。

senses.title: To aid in a lesser way
senses.definition: to give secondary or supporting help rather than main effort
senses.definitionCN: 提供次要的、配合性的帮助，而不是承担主要工作
senses.example: Each department is expected to subsidise the main relief effort.
senses.exampleCN: 每个部门都要为主要的救援行动提供辅助支持。
senses.why: Subsidium meant a secondary body of troops, so the verb once meant to back someone up in a smaller role.
senses.whyCN: subsidium 指次要的一队兵马，这个词因而曾表示「以次要身份配合支援」。

intro.en: Subsidise comes from Latin subsidium, a reserve of soldiers kept at the rear as support, formed from sub- (under, in reserve) and sedere (to sit).
intro.cn: subsidise 来自拉丁语 subsidium（留在后方待命的后备部队），由 sub-（在下、后备）与 sedere（坐）构成。

items.en: Latin sedere means to sit, giving the image of troops sitting in reserve.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为坐，由此形成「兵马坐在后备位置」的意象。

items.en: Subsidium names a reserve force that sits behind the battle line to help when needed.
items.cn: subsidium 指坐在战线后方、随时准备支援的后备部队。

items.en: The verb subsidere develops the sense of coming to the aid of another.
items.cn: 动词 subsidere 发展出「来援助他人」的意思。

items.en: English subsidy first means a payment of support to the crown.
items.cn: 英语 subsidy 最初指臣民向王室缴纳的支援性款项。

items.en: Money given by a government to keep prices low is called a subsidy.
items.cn: 政府为压低价格而拨给的钱开始被称为 subsidy。

items.en: The verb subsidise spreads in the 19th and 20th centuries with public funding of transport, health, and farming.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪，随着公共交通、医疗与农业获得公共资金，动词 subsidise 广泛使用。

note.en: Subsidise is the act of giving support money; subsidy is the money, and subsidised describes whatever receives it.
note.cn: subsidise 是「给补贴」这个动作，subsidy 是被给的那笔钱，subsidised 形容接受补贴的事物。

entries.definition: money paid by a government to lower a price or keep a service running
entries.definitionCN: 政府为压低价格或维持服务而发放的资金

entries.definition: connected with but less important, or a company owned by a larger one
entries.definitionCN: 附属的、次要的；也指子公司

entries.definition: receiving part of its cost from public money
entries.definitionCN: 部分费用由公共资金承担的

entries.definition: the idea that decisions should be taken at the lowest practical level
entries.definitionCN: 辅助原则，即决定应在尽可能低的层级作出

entries.definition: to provide the money needed for something
entries.definitionCN: 为某事提供所需资金

entries.definition: to supply money for a project or purchase
entries.definitionCN: 为项目或购买行为提供资金

entries.definition: to pay for an event in exchange for advertising
entries.definitionCN: 以换取宣传为条件出资赞助

entries.definition: to agree to pay the costs if something goes wrong
entries.definitionCN: 承诺承担某项支出的风险

normalIntro.en: Subsidise carries the Latin image of a reserve force sitting behind the line, ready to step in with money.
normalIntro.cn: subsidise 带着拉丁语「后备兵马坐在后方」的意象：一队人待命，随时带着钱来补位。

normal.en: Subsidise pairs with subsidy: the verb gives the money, the noun is the money.
normal.cn: subsidise 与 subsidy 成对：动词表示给钱，名词表示给的那笔钱。

normal.en: The sub- in subsidise means under or in reserve, as in submarine and substitute.
normal.cn: subsidise 里的 sub- 表示「在下、后备」，与 submarine、substitute 同前缀。

normal.en: Heavily subsidised means kept cheap by a lot of outside money.
normal.cn: heavily subsidised 表示靠着大量外来资金才保持低价。

normal.en: British writers use -ise while American writers spell it subsidize.
normal.cn: 英式写作拼作 -ise 结尾，美式拼作 subsidize。

normal.en: Governments subsidise what they want people to use more of, such as buses and solar panels.
normal.cn: 政府会补贴那些希望人们多用的事物，比如公交和太阳能板。

abstract.en: Picture a reserve troop sitting behind the hill, waiting to rush in and pay half the bill.
abstract.cn: 想象一队后备兵坐在山丘后面，随时冲出来替你付掉半张账单。

abstract.en: A price tag showing the real price crossed out, with a hand paying the difference below the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象价签上的原价被划掉，柜台下方有一只手悄悄替顾客补上差价。

abstract.en: A wallet with a coin slot marked from the government feeding a discount into the till.
abstract.cn: 想象一只政府钱包把折扣硬币送进收银机，让价钱变低。

examples.en: The government subsidises rail travel to keep cars off the roads.
examples.cn: 政府补贴铁路出行，以减少公路上的汽车。

examples.en: Without subsidised rent, many young teachers could not live near the school.
examples.cn: 如果没有租金补贴，许多年轻教师无法住在学校附近。

examples.en: Farmers argue that it is unfair to subsidise one crop but not another.
examples.cn: 农民认为只补贴一种作物而不补贴另一种是不公平的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「仨不塞袋」——补贴就是把钱往兜里塞；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下、后备）+ sedere（坐）→ subsidium（坐在后方待命的后备部队）→ 中世纪拉丁语 subsidium（援助、津贴）→ 英语 subsidy 与动词 subsidise，核心义「在背后垫钱支援」。

sensesIntro.en: Subsidise starts as money paid on behalf of someone else, widens to supporting an organisation, then covers making things affordable, paying for loyalty, and giving secondary help.
sensesIntro.cn: subsidise 从「替别人付掉一部分钱」出发，扩展到资助一个机构、让某物变得负担得起、用钱换支持，最后保留「从旁辅助」的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a reserve troop sitting behind the line, ready to send money forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：后备兵马坐在战线后方，随时把钱送上前线。

branches.en: Paying part of a cost is the everyday sense, closest to the reserve force image.
branches.cn: 替别人分担一部分费用是日常义项，最贴近后备兵马的意象。

branches.en: Keeping an organisation going is the cost-sharing idea applied to a whole activity.
branches.cn: 让机构维持运转，是把「分担费用」的观念扩展到一个完整活动上。

branches.en: Making something affordable focuses on the buyer who is spared part of the bill.
branches.cn: 使某物负担得起，把焦点放在因此少付一部分钱的购买者身上。

branches.en: Paying for loyalty keeps the image of money offered in exchange for support.
branches.cn: 用钱换忠诚，保留了「出钱换取支持」的意象。

branches.en: Giving secondary help is the oldest layer, where one body backs up another.
branches.cn: 提供次要帮助是最古老的一层，指一支部队支援另一支部队。

intro.en: Subsidise is built on the Latin root sedere, to sit, behind the prefix sub-, together with subsidy, subsidiary, and the suffix -ise.
intro.cn: subsidise 由拉丁词根 sedere（坐）与前缀 sub- 构成，并与 subsidy、subsidiary 以及后缀 -ise 同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- means under or in reserve, and sedere means to sit; subsidium is a force that sits behind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 意为「在下、后备」，sedere 意为「坐」；subsidium 就是坐在后方的那支兵马。

items.example: The prefix sub- gives the idea of support from below.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 带来「从下方支援」的意味。

items.example: Sedere supplies the image of troops waiting in place.
items.exampleCN: sedere 提供兵马原地待命的画面。

items.example: Subsidium is the direct source of the word.
items.exampleCN: subsidium 是这个词的直接来源。

items.meaning: money paid to support a price or service
items.example: A subsidy is the money that is paid.
items.exampleCN: subsidy 指被支付的那笔钱。

items.example: The suffix -ise turns the noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 把名词变成动词。

items.meaningCN: 美式拼写中与 -ise 对应的词尾
items.example: American English writes subsidize with -ize.
items.exampleCN: 美式英语写作 subsidize。

items.meaning: to pay part of a cost
items.example: Subsidise names the act of giving support money.
items.exampleCN: subsidise 指发放支援资金的行动。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms subsidised.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 subsidised。

items.example: Subsidised housing is cheaper because part of the cost is paid.
items.exampleCN: 补贴住房更便宜，因为一部分成本已被支付。

items.example: The ending -ary gives subsidiary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成 subsidiary。

latinEntries.meaning: to sit down, to come to help

definition_zh: 证实；证明；用证据支持；使具体化
definition_en: to provide evidence that proves something is true
core_image: 一张空泛的说法被一张张票据和照片垫实，从空话变成实体
scene: 记者要求部长拿出文件，证明他关于预算的说法。The reporter asked the minister to substantiate her claim about the budget.
sceneCN: 这里 substantiate 是「证实、用证据支持」（第 1 个义项：提供证据证明某事为真）；句意：记者要求部长为她关于预算的说法提供证据。

pos.zh: 证实；证明；用证据支持；使具体化

collocations.zh: 以数据为依据得到证实

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 substantia（本质、实体）而来，指物质、实质；是 substantiate 的构词基础
由 substantiate 加 -ion 构成，指证实的过程或所提供的证据
由 substantiate 加 -ed 构成，指已被证实有据的
由拉丁语 substantivus 而来，指实质性的、有实体的
由拉丁语 substantialis 而来，指大量的、坚固的、实质的
由否定的 in- 加 substantial 构成，指虚幻的、不结实的

senses.title: To prove with evidence
senses.definition: to prove that a statement or claim is true by giving evidence
senses.definitionCN: 通过提供证据，证明某个说法或主张的真实性
senses.example: The study substantiates what earlier researchers had guessed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究证实了早期研究者的猜测。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to give substance to a thing, so proving a claim gives it real weight instead of thin talk.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本义是给事物加上实体，因此证实一个说法就是让它有分量，而不只是空话。

senses.title: To give solid form to an idea
senses.definition: to turn something abstract into a form that can be seen or handled
senses.definitionCN: 把抽象的东西变成看得见、摸得着的形式
senses.example: The architect substantiated the plan with models and drawings.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师用模型和图纸把计划具体化。
senses.why: Substance is what gives something standing, so the verb can mean giving a plan or idea real shape.
senses.whyCN: substance 是让事物立得起来的东西，因此这个动词也可以指给计划或想法以真实形态。

senses.title: To support a position in law
senses.definition: to offer enough evidence in a legal case to back a charge or defence
senses.definitionCN: 在法律案件中提供足够证据，支持某项指控或辩护
senses.example: The prosecutor could not substantiate the charge of fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 检方无法为欺诈指控提供证据。
senses.why: Courts decide whether a charge has substance, so the legal sense asks whether evidence can stand the claim up.
senses.whyCN: 法院要判断一项指控是否有实质内容，法律义项就是问证据能否把指控支撑起来。

senses.title: To make real or actual
senses.definition: to cause something to become real rather than only planned
senses.definitionCN: 使某事由计划变成现实
senses.example: The new law substantiates the rights promised in the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律使条约中承诺的权利成为现实。
senses.why: What has substance exists, so the verb stretches from proving to making something exist in practice.
senses.whyCN: 有实体即意味着存在，于是这个动词从「证明」延伸到「在实践中使之存在」。

intro.en: Substantiate comes from Latin substantia, substance, built from sub- (under) and stare (to stand), and passed to English through the Latin verb substantiare, to give substance.
intro.cn: substantiate 来自拉丁语 substantia（实体、本质），由 sub-（在下）与 stare（站立）构成，经拉丁语动词 substantiare（赋予实体）进入英语。

items.en: The root stare means to stand, so substance is what stands beneath a thing.
items.cn: 词根 stare 意为站立，因此 substance 就是「站在事物下面的东西」。

items.en: Substantia translates the Greek notion of underlying being, into which earlier Greek writers put the idea of standing under.
items.cn: substancia 用来翻译希腊语中「底层存在」的概念，希腊作家用「立于其下」表达这层意思。

items.en: The verb substantiare means to give substance or to make something stand.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语动词 substantiare 意为赋予实体、使某物立起来。

items.en: English substantiate first means to give real form to something.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语中，substantiate 最初意为「使某物具有真实形态」。

items.en: The sense of proving a claim with evidence becomes the dominant one.
items.cn: 「用证据证明某项主张」的义项逐渐成为主导。

items.en: Today the verb appears most in the phrases substantiate a claim and substantiate an allegation.
items.cn: 今天这个词最常见于「证实某项说法」与「证实某项指控」这两种搭配。

note.en: Substantiate is the word of giving real weight to a claim; substance is the weight itself, and substantiation is the evidence offered.
note.cn: substantiate 是「给说法加上真实分量」的动作；substance 是那份分量本身，substantiation 则指所提出的证据。

entries.definition: a material or the real quality of something
entries.definitionCN: 物质；实质、内容

entries.definition: large in amount, or solid and real
entries.definitionCN: 大量的；实实在在的

entries.definition: real and important rather than formal
entries.definitionCN: 实质性的、重要的（而非形式上的）

entries.definition: evidence that proves a claim
entries.definitionCN: 证明某项主张的证据

entries.definition: to check that something is accurate or true
entries.definitionCN: 核对、检验某事是否准确属实

entries.definition: to say that something is definitely true
entries.definitionCN: 确认某事确实为真

entries.definition: to support a statement with more evidence from another source
entries.definitionCN: 用另一来源的证据进一步佐证

entries.definition: to show beyond doubt that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 证明某事毫无疑问地为真

normalIntro.en: Substantiate is substance plus the verb ending -ate: to put substance under a claim until it can stand.
normalIntro.cn: substantiate 是 substance 加上动词词尾 -ate：把一个说法底下垫上实体，让它立得住。

normal.en: Substantiate a claim is the classic pattern, often followed by with evidence.
normal.cn: substantiate a claim 是经典搭配，后面常接 with evidence。

normal.en: The family shares the root stare, to stand, seen in substance, substantial, and substantiate.
normal.cn: 这一词族共用词根 stare（站立），即 substance、substantial 与 substantiate。

normal.en: The noun substantiation names the evidence brought forward.
normal.cn: 名词 substantiation 指被拿出来的那份证据。

normal.en: Journalists use fail to substantiate when someone cannot back up a claim.
normal.cn: 记者用 fail to substantiate 表示某人拿不出证据支持自己的说法。

normal.en: Compare verify: you verify a fact, but you substantiate a claim or an allegation.
normal.cn: 对比 verify：verify 核对的是事实，substantiate 支撑的是主张或指控。

abstract.en: Picture a thin sheet of paper gaining weight as receipts are taped to it one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张薄纸被一张张贴上票据，越来越沉、越来越实。

abstract.en: Imagine a claim written in air, then a table pushed under it so it rests on something real.
abstract.cn: 想象一句悬浮在空中的说法，有人在它下面推来一张桌子，让它落到实处。

abstract.en: A lawyer holds up a folder that grows until a charge can finally stand on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象律师举起一个越来越厚的文件夹，直到一项指控终于站得住。

examples.en: More data are needed to substantiate the link between the two events.
examples.cn: 需要更多数据才能证实这两个事件之间的联系。

examples.en: She was unable to substantiate her complaint, so it was dropped.
examples.cn: 她无法为自己的投诉提供证据，投诉遂被撤销。

examples.en: The body of an article is where the writer substantiates each claim.
examples.cn: 文章的正文是作者逐一证实其主张的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「实舔一帖」——贴上实在的证据，说法才站得住；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ stare（站立）→ substantia（站在事物下面的东西；实体、本质）→ 晚期拉丁语动词 substantiare（赋予实体）→ 英语 substantiate，核心义「在说法底下垫上实体」。

sensesIntro.en: Substantiate grows from giving a thing real substance: it first proves a claim with evidence, then gives shape to a plan, backs a charge in court, and finally makes something real.
sensesIntro.cn: substantiate 的出发点是为事物加上实体：先是用证据证实一个说法，再是把计划变成看得见的形态，接着是在法庭上为指控举证，最后是使某事成为现实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table pushed under a floating claim so that it rests on something solid.
core.cn: 核心意象：在悬浮的说法下面推来一张桌子，让它落在实处。

branches.en: Proving with evidence is the central sense of the modern verb.
branches.cn: 用证据证实是现代用法的中心义项。

branches.en: Giving solid form to an idea keeps the literal image of adding substance.
branches.cn: 让想法获得实体形态，保留了「加上实体」的字面意象。

branches.en: Legal use asks whether a charge can stand on the evidence offered.
branches.cn: 法律用法追问一项指控能否靠所给证据立得住。

branches.en: Both ordinary proofs and court proofs turn words into supported claims.
branches.cn: 日常举证与法庭举证都把话语变成有支撑的主张。

branches.en: Making a plan concrete and making a right real share the idea of turning possibility into substance.
branches.cn: 把计划具体化与让权利成为现实，都体现把可能性变成实体的思路。

intro.en: Substantiate is built on sub- and the Latin root sta, to stand, with the verb ending -ate; its family includes substance, substantial, and substantive.
intro.cn: substantiate 由前缀 sub-、拉丁词根 sta（站立）与动词词尾 -ate 构成，同族词有 substance、substantial 与 substantive。

latinIntro.en: Latin substare means to stand under, and substantia is what stands under a thing; substantiare means to give substance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 substare 意为「立于其下」，substantia 即站在事物下面的东西；substantiare 意为「赋予实体」。

items.example: The prefix sub- places the support underneath.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把支撑放在下方。

items.example: The root sta gives the image of something standing.
items.exampleCN: 词根 sta 带来「站立」的意象。

items.example: Substantia is the source of the English family.
items.exampleCN: substantia 是这组英语词的来源。

items.example: Substantiare supplies the verb sense of giving substance.
items.exampleCN: substantiare 提供「赋予实体」的动词义。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms verbs such as substantiate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 substantiate 这类动词。

items.example: Substance names the real quality of a thing.
items.exampleCN: substance 指事物的实质。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms substantial.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 构成 substantial。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms substantive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 substantive。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms substantiation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 substantiation。

items.example: The prefix in- forms insubstantial.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 insubstantial。

definition_zh: 字幕；副标题；给…加字幕
definition_en: words shown at the bottom of a screen that translate or describe the speech, or a second title under the main one
core_image: 电影画面最底下一行白色小字，跟着人物的话一行行滚过
scene: 一段外语纪录片找不到配音演员，电视台就在画面底部加上字幕。The channel added English subtitles to the foreign documentary about rare birds.
sceneCN: 这里 subtitle 是「字幕」（第 1 个义项：显示在画面底部、翻译对白或说明内容的文字）；句意：这家电视台为那部关于珍稀鸟类的外国语纪录片加上了英文字幕。

derivatives.zh: 由 subtitle 加 -ed 构成，指配有字幕的，或带有副标题的
由 subtitle 加 -ing 构成，指字幕制作这一行当或工作
由 subtitle 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，指字幕翻译员
subtitle 由前缀 sub- 加 title 构成，title 本义为标题、名称
由 super-（在上）加 title 构成，指显示在舞台上方的大投影字幕

senses.title: Words on the screen
senses.definition: words shown at the bottom of a film or programme that translate or repeat what is said
senses.definitionCN: 显示在影片或节目底部、翻译或记录所说内容的文字
senses.example: The DVD has English subtitles and a French soundtrack.
senses.exampleCN: 这张光盘有英文字幕和法语配音。
senses.why: A subtitle is a caption sitting under the picture, so the word first names the text that supports the spoken sound from below.
senses.whyCN: subtitle 本义是「写在下面的题名」，因此第一次要就是指从画面下方支撑声音的文字。

senses.title: A second title
senses.definition: a secondary title written below the main title of a book or work
senses.definitionCN: 写在书籍或作品主标题下方、起补充说明作用的标题
senses.example: The subtitle of the book is a short history of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书的副标题是「一部关于水的简史」。
senses.why: The Latin prefix sub- means under, so a subtitle is literally a title placed beneath another title.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 sub- 意为「在下」，所以副标题字面上就是放在另一个标题下面的标题。

senses.title: The act of subtitling
senses.definition: to add screen text to a film or programme
senses.definitionCN: 为影片或节目添加屏幕文字
senses.example: The studio subtitled the show for viewers abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 制作方为海外观众给节目配上了字幕。
senses.why: From the noun meaning screen text grows a verb: to subtitle a film is to put that text there.
senses.whyCN: 由「屏幕文字」这一名词义发展出动词义：给影片加字幕就是把这些文字放上去。

senses.title: A line added under a heading
senses.definition: a short explanatory line beneath a headline or chapter heading
senses.definitionCN: 标题或章节名下方起解释作用的短行文字
senses.example: Under the headline ran a subtitle in smaller type.
senses.exampleCN: 大标题下方有一行字号更小的副题。
senses.why: Printers used the same word for any line set beneath a bigger line, so the sense spreads to news and chapter layout.
senses.whyCN: 印刷者用同一个词称呼任何排在大字下方的一行，于是这个词也扩展到报纸标题与章节排版。

intro.en: Subtitle joins the Latin prefix sub- (under) to title, which comes from Latin titulus, a label or inscription.
intro.cn: subtitle 由拉丁语前缀 sub-（在下）加 title 构成，而 title 来自拉丁语 titulus（题签、标牌）。

items.en: Titulus means a label, a notice, or a name given to a thing.
items.cn: titulus 意为标签、告示，或给事物起的名称。

items.en: The prefix sub- means under, forming compounds that place one thing below another.
items.cn: 前缀 sub- 意为「在下」，常构成「把一物放在另一物下面」的复合词。

items.en: Title enters English from Old French in the sense of an inscription or heading.
items.cn: title 经古法语进入英语，意为题铭或标题。

items.en: Subtitle names an explanatory second title printed below a book title.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语中，subtitle 指印在书名下方起解释作用的第二个标题。

items.en: With silent film and then talkies, subtitle comes to mean the translated words at the foot of the screen.
items.cn: 随着默片和有声电影出现，subtitle 开始指银幕底部翻译对白的文字。

items.en: Streaming services and captioning software make subtitling a mass activity, with its own job title subtitler.
items.cn: 流媒体与字幕软件让字幕制作成为大众行业，还专门有了 subtitle 加 -er 构成的职业称呼。

note.en: Subtitle is literally a title underneath: under the headline on a page, or under the picture on a screen.
note.cn: subtitle 字面上就是「下面的题名」：或在一页标题之下，或在屏幕画面之下。

entries.definition: the name given to a book, film, or other work
entries.definitionCN: 书名、片名等作品的名称

entries.definition: having text at the bottom of the screen
entries.definitionCN: 配有屏幕字幕的

entries.definition: the work or process of adding screen text
entries.definitionCN: 字幕制作这一工作或过程

entries.definition: large text projected above an opera stage
entries.definitionCN: 歌剧舞台上方投射的大字字幕

entries.definition: a short text printed under a picture or shown on screen
entries.definitionCN: 图片下方的说明文字，或屏幕上的文字说明

entries.definition: replacing the voices of a film with another language
entries.definitionCN: 用另一种语言替换影片配音

entries.definition: the title at the top of a page or section
entries.definitionCN: 页面或章节顶端的标题

entries.definition: a written version of spoken words
entries.definitionCN: 口语内容的文字记录

normalIntro.en: Subtitle is simply sub plus title: a title under another title, and by extension words under a picture.
normalIntro.cn: subtitle 就是 sub 加 title：一个标题放在另一个标题下面，引申为画面下面的文字。

normal.en: The sub- in subtitle means under, as in submarine and subsoil.
normal.cn: subtitle 里的 sub- 意为「在下」，与 submarine、subsoil 同前缀。

normal.en: With subtitles means the original voices stay and text appears below.
normal.cn: with subtitles 表示保留原声、在下方显示文字。

normal.en: Subtitle is both noun and verb: you add subtitles, and you subtitle a film.
normal.cn: subtitle 既是名词又是动词：你既 add subtitles，也 subtitle a film。

normal.en: Compare caption: a caption explains a picture, a subtitle translates speech.
normal.cn: 对比 caption：caption 解释图片，subtitle 翻译台词。

normal.en: A book subtitle sits under the main title and tells you what the book is really about.
normal.cn: 书的副标题位于主标题下方，告诉你这本书真正讲的是什么。

abstract.en: Picture a white line of text running under the actors as they speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一行白色文字在演员开口时从他们脚下滚过。

abstract.en: Imagine a big title and a smaller title tucked right underneath it, like a smaller hat under a bigger one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个大标题下面塞着一个小标题，就像大帽子下垫着一顶小帽子。

abstract.en: A finger presses a remote button and the bottom strip of the screen lights up with language.
abstract.cn: 想象手指按下遥控器，屏幕底部那一条亮起了另一种语言。

examples.en: Turn on the subtitles so we can follow the dialogue.
examples.cn: 把字幕打开，这样我们能跟上对白。

examples.en: The series was subtitled rather than dubbed for its international release.
examples.cn: 这部剧在海外发行时采用字幕而非配音。

examples.en: Her essay carries the subtitle notes from a broken city.
examples.cn: 她的文章带有一个副标题「来自一座破碎之城的笔记」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨布台头」——字幕总在画面底下，演员的「台头」反而看不清；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ titulus（题签、标牌）→ 古法语 title（题铭、标题）→ 英语前缀 sub- 加 title 构成 subtitle，核心义「写在下方的那行题名」。

sensesIntro.en: Subtitle begins as a title placed under another, then moves to the screen: the text under a picture, the act of adding it, and the small line under a heading.
sensesIntro.cn: subtitle 起初指放在另一个标题下方的标题，后来转到屏幕上：画面下方的文字、给画面加文字的动作，以及排在大标题下方的小字行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of text sitting under the main line, whether a title under a title or words under a picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：一行文字安在大字的下面，无论是标题下的标题，还是画面下的对白。

branches.en: Screen text is the dominant sense in everyday use.
branches.cn: 屏幕文字是日常使用中最主要的义项。

branches.en: The second title is the oldest sense and the literal meaning of the parts.
branches.cn: 副标题是最古老的义项，也是各部分字面意思的直译。

branches.en: The verb sense grew from the noun once the text had a name.
branches.cn: 动词义在名词义站稳之后才发展出来。

branches.en: Small print lines under headlines extend the under-a-title idea into print.
branches.cn: 大标题下的小字行，把「标题之下」的想法延伸到印刷版面。

branches.en: The noun names the text, and the verb is the act of putting it there.
branches.cn: 名词指那些文字，动词指把文字放上去的动作。

intro.en: Subtitle is a transparent compound of the Latin prefix sub- and title, with derived forms subtitled, subtitling, and subtitler.
intro.cn: subtitle 是拉丁语前缀 sub- 与 title 明明白白的组合词，派生形式有 subtitled、subtitling 与 subtitler。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- means under, and titulus means a label or inscription; together they give the idea of a title placed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 意为「在下」，titulus 意为标签或题铭；两者合起来就是「放在下面的题名」。

items.example: The prefix sub- puts the text below.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把文字放在下面。

items.example: Titulus is the root of title.
items.exampleCN: titulus 是 title 的词根。

items.example: Title is the base of the compound.
items.exampleCN: title 是这个复合词的基础。

items.meaning: screen text or a second title
items.example: Subtitle is the compound itself.
items.exampleCN: subtitle 就是这个词本身。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms subtitled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 subtitled。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms subtitling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 subtitling。

items.example: The suffix -er forms subtitler.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 subtitler。

items.example: A subtitler keeps each line short enough to read.
items.exampleCN: 字幕员会让每一行短到能读完。

items.example: The prefix super- forms supertitle, the opposite of a subtitle.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 super- 构成 supertitle，正好与 subtitle 相对。

items.meaningCN: 墙上或舞台上方的字幕
items.example: Supertitle uses above where subtitle uses under.
items.exampleCN: supertitle 用的是「在上」，subtitle 用的是「在下」。

definition_zh: 微妙的；细微的；巧妙的；敏锐的；隐约的
definition_en: so delicate or slight that it is easy to miss; clever in a quiet way; able to notice fine differences
core_image: 浅色墙上一道极淡的接缝，只有把脸贴近或从侧面看，才看得见那条细细的纹路
scene: 画展上两幅作品的色彩几乎一样，参观者几乎看不出差别。The difference between the two paintings is so subtle that most visitors miss it.
sceneCN: 这里 subtle 是「微妙的；不易察觉的」（第 1 个义项：差别细微得几乎看不出来）；句意：这两幅画的差别太微妙，大多数参观者都看不出来。

pos.zh: 微妙的；细微的；不易察觉的
隐约的；淡淡的（气味、味道）

derivatives.zh: 由 subtle 加 -ly 构成，义为「微妙地；不易察觉地；巧妙地」
由 subtle 加 -ty 构成，义为「微妙；细微差别；精妙之处」
由 subtil（subtle 的古拼写）加 -ize 构成，义为「使过细；在细处过分推敲」
subtlety 的旧式拼写，保留拉丁语 subtilitas 的词形，多见于早期英文作品

senses.title: Too slight to be noticed at once
senses.definition: very small and delicate, so that it is hard to see or describe
senses.definitionCN: 极细微而精巧，难以看见或说清
senses.example: There is a subtle difference between the two shades of blue.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种蓝色之间有着微妙的差别。
senses.why: Subtle descends from the Latin adjective subtilis, woven fine, so the first sense is a difference as thin as a finely woven thread.
senses.whyCN: subtle 源自拉丁语形容词 subtilis（织得细密），所以第一个义项就是像细线一样几乎看不见的细微差别。

senses.title: Clever or skillful without showing off
senses.definition: done with quiet skill, so that the cleverness is not obvious
senses.definitionCN: 以不张扬的技巧做成，聪明之处并不显眼
senses.example: She solved the problem with a subtle and elegant plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一个巧妙而优雅的方案解决了问题。
senses.why: A finely woven thing is hard to see through, and a finely made plan hides its own cleverness, which gives the sense of skill that does not shout.
senses.whyCN: 织得细密的东西难以穿透，精细做出的方案也把自己的聪明藏了起来，于是引申出「不张扬的有技巧」。

senses.title: Able to tell small differences
senses.definition: able to notice and judge very small differences, usually of the senses or the mind
senses.definitionCN: 能察觉并判断极细微的差别，多指感官或心思
senses.example: Master tea tasters have a subtle sense of taste.
senses.exampleCN: 首席评茶师对味道有敏锐的分辨力。
senses.why: The person whose senses can tell one fine thread from another becomes subtle in mind, so the adjective also names keen perception.
senses.whyCN: 能分清一根细线与另一根细线的人，在心思上也算 subtle，于是这个词又指敏锐的感知力。

senses.title: Faint and hard to notice, of smell or taste
senses.definition: light and not strong, recognized only if you pay attention, especially of a smell or flavour
senses.definitionCN: 清淡而不浓烈，须留心才辨得出，多指气味或味道
senses.example: The kitchen carried a subtle smell of cinnamon.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房里飘着淡淡的肉桂香。
senses.why: The finely woven sense returns to the body, giving a smell or taste so light that it stays near the edge of notice.
senses.whyCN: 「织得细」的意象回到身体层面，就是淡到几乎只停在注意边缘的气味或味道。

senses.title: Careful and indirect, of a hint or warning
senses.definition: expressed gently, so that the message reaches the listener without being blunt
senses.definitionCN: 表达得温和克制，信息传达出去却不直白刺人
senses.example: He gave her a subtle warning about the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 他委婉地提醒了她截止日期。
senses.why: Quiet skill applied to speech becomes the sense of a message whose edge is softened, so the listener feels the point without feeling attacked.
senses.whyCN: 把「悄悄的技巧」用在言语上，就是语气被磨钝的信息，听者能领会要点却不觉得被冒犯。

senses.title: The quality of being difficult to grasp
senses.titleCN: （名词化）微妙之处；难以把握的地方
senses.definition: the quality of something that is hard to measure, prove or put into plain words
senses.definitionCN: 难以衡量、证明或用平白语言说清的性质
senses.example: The subtlety of the argument escaped most reviewers.
senses.exampleCN: 这一论证的精妙之处多数评论者都没看出来。
senses.why: Once a thing is too fine for plain words, the adjective turns back into a noun, and subtlety names that slippery quality itself.
senses.whyCN: 当一件事细到无法用平白的话说明时，这个形容词又变回名词，subtlety 就指这种难以捉摸的性质本身。

intro.en: Subtle comes from the Latin adjective subtilis, a word for cloth woven so finely that it is hard to see through. The b was added in English from the Latin spelling.
intro.cn: subtle 来自拉丁语形容词 subtilis，原指织得极细、几乎透不过的布；英语中的 b 是先按拉丁拼写补进去的，并不发音。

items.en: Subtilis describes cloth woven with fine threads and also fine judgement.
items.cn: subtilis 既描述细线织成的布，也指精细的判断。

items.en: In late Latin subtilis extends to arguments and to things that are hard to separate.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把 subtilis 扩展到论证以及难以分辨的事物。

items.en: Old French sotil and soutil drop the b and give English its sound.
items.cn: 古法语 sotil 与 soutil 丢掉 b，给英语带来现在的读音。

items.en: English first writes the word as sotil and uses it for finely made cloth and clever speech.
items.cn: 中古英语早期写作 sotil，用来形容做工细致的布与聪明的言辞。

items.en: Learned spelling restores the Latin b, so subtle is now written with a letter that is silent.
items.cn: 十六世纪学者式拼写把拉丁的 b 还原回来，于是 subtle 多了一个不发音的字母。

items.en: The word settles on slight differences, quiet skill, and keen perception.
items.cn: 现代英语把它固定为细微差别、含蓄技巧与敏锐感知三层意思。

note.en: The first group holds the sub- Latin family and the words most often confused with subtle; the second holds adjectives for things that are hard to see or state.
note.cn: 第一组是拉丁前缀 sub- 的同族词，以及与 subtle 最常混淆的形近词；第二组是其他表示「不易看见或不易说清」的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being subtle, or a small fine difference.
entries.definitionCN: 表示微妙性质的抽象名词，或指细微的差别。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a way that is hard to notice.
entries.definitionCN: 表示以不易察觉的方式做某事的副词。

entries.definition: To take a number away from another; only the Latin prefix sub- is shared.
entries.definitionCN: 把数目相减，只与 subtle 共享拉丁前缀 sub-，词根不同。

entries.definition: Text shown at the bottom of a screen; built on sub- plus title, not on subtle.
entries.definitionCN: 屏幕下方显示的字幕，由 sub- 加 title 构成，与 subtle 词源无关。

entries.definition: A common misspelling that swaps the b and t; the correct order is b then t.
entries.definitionCN: 常见的错误拼写，把 b 与 t 颠倒了，正确的是 b 在前 t 在后。

entries.definition: Small in degree, but it says nothing about being hard to notice.
entries.definitionCN: 程度上小，但不包含「难以察觉」的意思。

entries.definition: Fine in texture or touch, often with a hint of fragility.
entries.definitionCN: 质地上细致，常带脆弱感。

entries.definition: Showing careful attention to small differences of feeling or meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 体现出对情感或意义细微差别的细心分辨。

entries.definition: Very weak, said of light, sound or smell that almost disappears.
entries.definitionCN: 极微弱，形容几乎消失的光、声或气味。

normalIntro.en: Two clues fix this word: the silent b, and the image of cloth woven too fine to see through.
normalIntro.cn: 两把钥匙：不发音的 b，以及「织得太细、透不过光」这块布。

normal.en: The b in subtle is a spelling relic of Latin and is never pronounced.
normal.cn: subtle 里的 b 是拉丁拼写的遗迹，从不发音。

normal.en: Subtlety and subtly keep the same silent b, so all three words sound like suttle.
normal.cn: subtlety 与 subtly 同样不发音，三个词都读成「suttle」。

normal.en: A subtle difference is one you need to look twice to find.
normal.cn: a subtle difference 指要再看一眼才能找到的差别。

normal.en: Subtle humour is clever but never loud.
normal.cn: subtle humour 是聪明却不吵闹的幽默。

normal.en: Compare vague: vague means unclear, subtle means fine and exact yet easy to miss.
normal.cn: 对比 vague：vague 是说不清，subtle 是精细准确却容易错过。

abstract.en: Hold a fabric up to the window and find a thread you can only see from the side.
abstract.cn: 把一块布举向窗口，找到一根只有侧看才看得见的线。

abstract.en: Hear a joke whose punch is so quiet that half the table laughs a second late.
abstract.cn: 听一个包袱很轻的笑话，半桌人要晚一秒才笑出来。

abstract.en: Picture a door painted almost the same white as the wall, so visitors walk past it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门刷成几乎与墙同样的白色，客人也就走了过去。

examples.en: There is a subtle difference in tone between the two letters.
examples.cn: 这两封信的语气有微妙的差别。

examples.en: The novel is held together by subtle humour and quiet sympathy.
examples.cn: 这部小说靠含蓄的幽默与安静的同情维系在一起。

examples.en: A good mechanic can hear a subtle change in the engine.
examples.cn: 好机修工能听出发动机里细微的变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒腿」——撒腿就跑的人，脚步声轻得你几乎听不见；subtle 就是这种细微、不易察觉。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 subtilis（织得细密的）→ 古法语 sotil、soutil（丢掉 b）→ 中古英语 sotil → 十六世纪按拉丁拼写补回不发音的 b → 现代英语 subtle，核心义「细到几乎看不见」。

sensesIntro.en: Subtle starts from a cloth woven fine enough to hide what lies behind it, then covers small differences, quiet skill, keen senses, faint smells, gentle hints, and the noun sense for what is hard to state.
sensesIntro.cn: subtle 从一块细到能挡住视线的布出发，依次发展出细微差别、含蓄的技巧、敏锐的感官、淡淡的气味、委婉的提示，最后名词化为「难以说清的微妙之处」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seam so faint that you must look from the side to see it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道淡得要从侧面才看得见的接缝。

branches.en: A fine weave hides itself, which becomes a difference that is easy to miss.
branches.cn: 细密的织法自我隐藏，引申为容易错过的小差别。

branches.en: Skill that hides itself is the clever use.
branches.cn: 把技巧藏起来，就是「巧妙、精细」的用法。

branches.en: A mind that can tell one thread from another has keen perception.
branches.cn: 能分清经纬的心思，就是敏锐的辨别力。

branches.en: Faint smells and gentle hints both stay at the edge of notice.
branches.cn: 淡淡的气味与委婉的提示都停在注意的边缘。

branches.en: When the difference cannot be put into plain words, it turns into a named subtlety.
branches.cn: 当差别无法用平白的话说出，就成了被命名的「微妙之处」。

intro.en: The Latin root subtilis yields the verb subtilize plus the modern adverbs and nouns, with sub- also living on in many separate words.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根 subtilis 派生出动词 subtilize 以及现代的副词、名词；前缀 sub- 也继续活在许多各自独立的词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin subtilis is the adjective for fine weaving and fine judgement, and subtilitas is the noun for that fineness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 subtilis 是形容细织与精判的形容词，subtilitas 是由它构成的名词。

items.example: The English form restored a silent Latin letter.
items.exampleCN: 英语词形补回了一个不发音的拉丁字母。

items.meaning: in a way that is hard to notice
items.example: The -ly ending turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.meaningCN: 性质或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix forms subtlety.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 subtlety。

items.meaningCN: 微妙；细微差别；精妙之处
items.example: Subtlety keeps the silent b.
items.exampleCN: subtlety 同样保留不发音的 b。

items.meaning: to make over-fine or reason too finely
items.meaningCN: 使过细；在细处过分推敲
items.example: The ending -ize builds a verb from the older stem subtil.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 由旧词干 subtil 构成动词。

items.meaningCN: 不含 b 的旧式拼写
items.example: Early texts write subtil for the same adjective.
items.exampleCN: 早期文本用 subtil 表示同一个形容词。

items.example: The prefix sub- also begins subtract and subtitle.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 还出现在 subtract 与 subtitle 开头。

items.meaningCN: 英语中不重读的收尾音节
items.example: The ending -tle never adds a separate syllable after the t.
items.exampleCN: 收尾的 -tle 不在 t 后另加音节。

items.example: The French form supplied the modern sound.
items.exampleCN: 法语词形提供了现代读音。

definition_zh: 屈服；屈从；抵挡不住；病倒；死去
definition_en: to yield to something stronger, such as pressure, illness or temptation, or to die of an illness
core_image: 一个人被重物压得双膝弯下，终于坐到地上，放弃抵抗
scene: 连续几天高强度的训练之后，队里最壮的运动员也累得站不稳。After days of hard training, even the strongest athlete succumbed to exhaustion.
sceneCN: 这里 succumb 是「（被某事）压倒；抵挡不住」（第 3 个义项：身体承受不住）；句意：连续几天高强度的训练之后，即使最强壮的运动员也抵不住疲惫。

pos.zh: 屈服；屈从；抵挡不住（诱惑、压力、疾病等）

derivatives.zh: 由 succumb 加 -ent 构成，义为「平躺的；伏卧的」，植物学上也指平卧的茎
由 succumb 加 -ing 构成，义为「屈服；抵挡不住的过程」

senses.title: To yield to force or pressure
senses.definition: to stop resisting someone or something that is stronger
senses.definitionCN: 停止抵抗比自己更强势的一方
senses.example: The government succumbed to public pressure and changed the law.
senses.exampleCN: 政府迫于公众压力修改了法律。
senses.why: The Latin verb subcumbere joins sub, meaning under, to cumbere, meaning to lie down, so the first sense is simply lying down under a weight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 subcumbere 由 sub（在下方）与 cumbere（躺下）合成，所以第一个义项就是「在重量之下躺倒」。

senses.title: To give in to desire
senses.definition: to be unable to resist something you want, such as food, drink or a habit
senses.definitionCN: 无法抵抗自己想要的东西，如食物、酒或某种习惯
senses.example: He succumbed to temptation and ate the whole cake.
senses.exampleCN: 他抵制不住诱惑，把整块蛋糕都吃了。
senses.why: Temptation is a weight too, and the body that lies down under it has stopped holding itself upright.
senses.whyCN: 诱惑同样是一种重量，向它倒下的身体就是不再费力撑着站直的姿态。

senses.title: To be overcome by exhaustion or strain
senses.definition: to give way because the body or mind can take no more
senses.definitionCN: 因身体或精神再也撑不住而垮下来
senses.example: The hikers succumbed to fatigue after the long climb.
senses.exampleCN: 长途攀登之后，徒步者抵不住疲劳了。
senses.why: The image of lying down describes cheerfully here, because extreme tiredness makes the floor more inviting than standing.
senses.whyCN: 「躺下」的意象在这里变得自然，因为极度疲劳时地面比站立更诱人。

senses.title: To fall ill, or to die of an illness
senses.definition: to become seriously ill or to die from a disease, old age or cold
senses.definitionCN: 患上重病，或因疾病、年老、严寒而死去
senses.example: Three of the animals succumbed to the infection within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 有三只动物在一周内死于感染。
senses.why: Lying under a weight widens from resisting an enemy to the body finally giving way, which is how the word comes to mean dying of a disease.
senses.whyCN: 「在重量下躺倒」从抵抗敌人扩展到身体终于垮掉，于是这个词也可以表示因病去世。

senses.title: To lose a contest quietly
senses.definition: to lose to a better side in a match or contest, usually without a fight
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛或较量中输给更强的对手，往往没有还手之力
senses.example: The home side succumbed to a late goal.
senses.exampleCN: 主队被对手一记晚来的进球击败。
senses.why: Sport borrows the same picture, with a team that stops resisting a stronger opponent.
senses.whyCN: 体育报道借用了这幅相同的画面，指球队不再抵抗更强的对手。

senses.title: In heraldic description, to lie down
senses.definition: used in heraldry with the sense of lying down, often at a lion
senses.definitionCN: 纹章术语，意为卧伏，多用于形容狮子
senses.example: The stone shield shows a lion couchant, an old partner of succumbent.
senses.exampleCN: 石盾上的纹样是一只卧伏的狮子，正是古老词 succumbent 的搭配。
senses.why: Heraldry kept the older adjective with the same lying root, so the word was once written into coats of arms as a position.
senses.whyCN: 纹章学保留了带同一「躺」词根的老形容词，这个词曾作为纹章里的姿态被写进家徽。

senses.title: To yield to a fact or truth
senses.definition: to give up a position and accept that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 放弃原有立场，承认某事属实
senses.example: The committee finally succumbed to the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会最终接受了证据。
senses.why: After resisting a force in the world, the verb turns inward to mental resistance, such as a belief that will not hold out against evidence.
senses.whyCN: 在抵抗外界力量之后，这个动词转向内心，指某种信念终于无法招架证据。

intro.en: Succumb is a quiet reworking of Latin subcumbere, made up of sub, under, and cumbere, to lie down, in the late Latin spelling succumbere.
intro.cn: succumb 是对拉丁语 subcumbere 的轻声改写，晚期拉丁语作 succumbere，由 sub（在下方）与 cumbere（躺下）构成。

items.en: Cum-bere means to lie down or take one bed, from the root of cubare.
items.cn: cumbere 意为躺下或同榻而卧，词根与 cubare 相同。

items.en: Subcumbere, later succumbere, means to sink under a weight and also to yield.
items.cn: subcumbere 后作 succumbere，意为在重量下沉落，也指屈服。

items.en: Writers use the verb of a soldier who sinks down, an army that falls, and a patient who gives way to disease.
items.cn: 作家用它写倒下的士兵、溃败的军队和向疾病投降的病人。

items.en: The verb enters English, first in the medical sense of giving way to illness.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语，最早用作医学术语，指向疾病投降。

items.en: The general sense of yielding to pressure or temptation becomes common.
items.cn: 「向压力或诱惑屈服」的泛义在十七世纪通行起来。

items.en: Today succumb mostly appears in fixed phrases, such as succumb to illness, pressure or temptation.
items.cn: 现代英语中 succumb 多出现在固定搭配里，如 succumb to illness、pressure 或 temptation。

note.en: The first group holds words that share the Latin stem of falling or lying down; the second holds the more common verbs of yielding that replace succumb in speech.
note.cn: 第一组是共享拉丁语「倒下、躺下」词干的词；第二组是口语中常替代 succumb 的屈服类动词。

entries.definition: Lying down or resting, and in botany a stem that lies on the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 平躺休息的，植物学上也指伏卧地面的茎。

entries.definition: The simple past form, common in obituaries and medical reports.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，常见于讣告与医学报告。

entries.definition: Lying upon a duty, hence holding an office or resting as a duty.
entries.definitionCN: 压在职责之上，引申为在任的或作为职责的。

entries.definition: Lieing back or resting, used of posture and of bicycles.
entries.definitionCN: 向后躺卧休息的，用于姿势与自行车。

entries.definition: The plain verb for giving way under pressure or argument.
entries.definitionCN: 表在压力或争论下让步的常用动词。

entries.definition: The everyday phrasal verb for admitting defeat.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中表示认输让步的短语动词。

entries.definition: To hand over control openly, used of troops and weapons.
entries.definitionCN: 公开交出控制权，多用于部队与武器。

entries.definition: To die, often in a serious or archaic tone.
entries.definitionCN: 死亡，语气郑重或古旧。

entries.definition: To stop resisting an opponent and accept terms, often followed by to.
entries.definitionCN: 停止抵抗对手并接受条件，后面也常接 to。

normalIntro.en: One sound clue and one spelling rule carry this word: the silent b and the single m before -ed.
normalIntro.cn: 一条读音线索加一条拼写规则就够了：不发音的 b，以及加 -ed 时只写一个 m。

normal.en: The b in succumb is silent, so both syllables start with s.
normal.cn: succumb 的 b 不发音，两个音节都以 s 开头。

normal.en: The past tense is succumbed with one m; doubling the m is a common slip.
normal.cn: 过去式 succumbed 只有一个 m，写成双 m 是常见笔误。

normal.en: Succumb nearly always takes to: succumb to pressure, illness or temptation.
normal.cn: succumb 后几乎总接 to：向压力、疾病或诱惑投降。

normal.en: It is formal; in speech people say give in or give way.
normal.cn: 它偏正式，口语中人们多说 give in 或 give way。

normal.en: In medical writing, succumb to often means dying of a disease.
normal.cn: 在医学写作中，succumb to 常指因病去世。

abstract.en: Watch a wrestler whose knees fold slowly until he sits on the mat.
abstract.cn: 看一名摔跤手双膝慢慢弯曲，终于坐到垫子上。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge of old iron bending under a lorry until it touches the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一座旧铁桥被卡车压弯，最后碰到水面。

abstract.en: Feel a branch bend as snow gathers, until its tip touches the ground.
abstract.cn: 感受树枝在积雪下越压越低，直到枝尖点地。

examples.en: Many small firms succumbed to the economic downturn.
examples.cn: 许多小公司抵挡不住经济下滑而倒闭。

examples.en: She never succumbed to the pressure to change her findings.
examples.cn: 她从未屈服于要求她修改研究结论的压力。

examples.en: Several residents succumbed to the heat during the heatwave.
examples.cn: 热浪期间有几位居民因高温去世。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨坎布」——想象萨坎布被一块大石头压住，膝盖一弯就倒下了；succumb 就是被压得屈服、抵挡不住。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下方）＋ cumbere（躺下）→ 晚期拉丁语 succumbere（在重压下倒下；屈服）→ 十六世纪英语 succumb，核心义「在重压下躺倒」。

sensesIntro.en: One picture runs through every sense: something too heavy to hold up, so the body goes down under it, whether the weight is an army, a temptation, an illness or proof.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项共用一幅画面：有东西重得撑不住，身体于是倒下去；这个「重量」可以是军队、诱惑、疾病，也可以是证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: knees folding under a weight until the body lies down.
core.cn: 核心意象：双膝在重压下弯折，最后整个身体躺倒。

branches.en: The pressure sense is the plain picture of lying down under an enemy.
branches.cn: 压力义就是「在敌人之下躺倒」的本义。

branches.en: Desire works as a weight on the will.
branches.cn: 欲望对意志而言就是压下来的重量。

branches.en: Tiredness and disease are weights on the body itself.
branches.cn: 疲劳与疾病压在身体本身之上。

branches.en: A match and an argument are contested spaces where one side stops resisting.
branches.cn: 比赛与争论都是较量场，总有一方停止抵抗。

branches.en: Both describe losing to something bigger, with and without a fight.
branches.cn: 两者都指败给更强势的一方，只是有无对抗之别。

intro.en: The family around succumb is Latin in shape: sub- plus cumbere, with -ent working as the adjective ending.
intro.cn: 围绕 succumb 的词族是拉丁形状：sub- 加 cumbere，形容词结尾则是 -ent。

latinIntro.en: Latin cumbere or its variant cubare means to lie down, and compound forms with sub- and in- describe lying under or upon something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cumbere（异体 cubare）意为躺下，加 sub- 或 in- 的复合词表示躺在下方或上方。

items.example: The prefix sub- places the action underneath.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把动作放在下方。

items.example: The verb cumbere supplies the lying image.
items.exampleCN: 动词 cumbere 提供「躺下」的画面。

items.example: The form succumbere turns the b into double c in sound.
items.exampleCN: succumbere 在读音上把 b 变成了双 c。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或动作的形容词词尾
items.example: The ending -ent forms succumbent.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 构成 succumbent。

items.example: Botany uses the word for stems that lie flat.
items.exampleCN: 植物学用它形容平卧的茎。

items.example: The past form keeps a single m.
items.exampleCN: 过去式只保留一个 m。

items.example: The ing form often follows is or was.
items.exampleCN: 现在分词常跟在 is 或 was 后面。

items.example: The English verb is the bare stem.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词只用光杆词干。

items.example: The related cubare sits behind incubate.
items.exampleCN: 同源的 cubare 藏在 incubate 背后。

latinEntries.meaning: to lie upon, to press on

definition_zh: 吸盘；吸管状器官；易受骗的人；嫩芽；吸根；另加在鞋底上的防滑片；吸盘鱼
definition_en: an organ or device that holds on by suction; a person who is easily fooled; a shoot that grows from a root; a fish of the carp family
core_image: 章鱼触手上的一圈小吸盘，碰到什么就牢牢吸住，一拉就紧
scene: 集市上一个摊贩把手抽出来，让墨鱼吸盘贴着玻璃。He lifted the squid and pressed its suckers against the glass.
sceneCN: 这里 sucker 是「吸盘」（第 1 个义项：靠吸力贴住东西的器官或装置）；句意：他把墨鱼举起来，让吸盘贴住玻璃。

pos.zh: 发出吮吸声；欺骗（口语）；长出根出条

derivatives.zh: sucker 与 fish 合成的复合词，义为「吸盘鱼；䲟鱼」，后者借吸盘吸附在大鱼或船底
由 sucker punch 压缩而成，义为「冷不防出拳偷袭」
sucker 的基础动词，义为「吮吸；吸」，表示用口腔或器械产生吸力
由 suck 加 -ling 构成，义为「乳兽；还在吃奶的孩子」

senses.title: An organ that grips by suction
senses.definition: a part of the body that holds on to a surface by creating a vacuum
senses.definitionCN: 靠产生真空吸住表面的身体部位
senses.example: The squid grips the glass with dozens of suckers.
senses.exampleCN: 墨鱼用几十个吸盘紧紧吸住玻璃。
senses.why: A sucker takes its name from the verb suck, because it holds on by drawing air or water away and letting pressure press it fast.
senses.whyCN: sucker 的名字来自动词 suck，因为它靠抽走空气或水、让压力把自己压紧来吸住东西。

senses.title: Someone who swallows whatever is sold to them
senses.definition: a person who believes promises too easily and is cheated
senses.definitionCN: 太容易相信承诺、因而被欺骗的人
senses.example: Only a sucker would pay that much for a fake watch.
senses.exampleCN: 只有傻瓜才会花那么多钱买一块假表。
senses.why: A fool is pictured as someone whose lips are always open, so anything offered to them is sucked straight in.
senses.whyCN: 蠢人被想象成一个永远张着嘴的人，别人递什么，他都会直接吸进去。

senses.title: A shoot rising straight from a root
senses.definition: a new stem that grows from a root or from below the graft of a fruit tree
senses.definitionCN: 从根上或果树嫁接处以下长出的新枝
senses.example: Gardeners cut off every sucker below the graft.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁把嫁接处下方的根出条全部剪掉。
senses.why: The shoot draws food from the parent plant as if it were sucking at it, so botany borrowed the same sucking image.
senses.whyCN: 新枝像在吮吸母株的养分，所以植物学借用了同一个「吸」的意象。

senses.title: A piece added to the sole to stop slipping
senses.definition: a separate piece of rubber fixed under a shoe or boot for grip
senses.definitionCN: 为增加摩擦力而另钉在鞋或靴底下的橡胶片
senses.example: He nailed a leather sucker onto each heel.
senses.exampleCN: 他在每只鞋跟下钉了一片皮制防滑片。
senses.why: A patch pressed hard against the ground sticks like a sucking mouth, so the cobbler word for a grip pad came from the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 紧压在地面的垫片像一张吸着的嘴，于是鞋匠用语中表示防滑片的词也出自同一个动词。

senses.title: A bottom-feeding fish of the carp family
senses.definition: a common freshwater fish that feeds on the bottom, so named for its dragging mouth
senses.definitionCN: 在底部觅食的常见淡水鱼，因其吸着状的嘴而得名
senses.example: The river still holds catfish, carp and sucker.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河里还有鲶鱼、鲤鱼和吸盘鱼。
senses.why: The English name of the fish follows its looking as if it were sucking at the riverbed, and it is the source of the American slang.
senses.whyCN: 这种鱼在英语里得名，是因为它看起来像在吮吸河床；美国俚语正是从这里来的。

senses.title: A pump that pulls or lifts by suction
senses.definition: a device or pipe that draws a liquid or gas by suction rather than by pressure
senses.definitionCN: 靠吸力而非压力抽取液体或气体的装置或管路
senses.example: A sucker lifts water from the ditch into the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 吸泵把沟里的水抽进贮水箱。
senses.why: Suck has also named devices that pull by vacuum since the nineteenth century, and sucker follows as the plain noun for such a pump.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪起 suck 也用来指依靠真空抽取的器械，sucker 便顺理成章成为这类吸泵的朴素名词。

senses.title: In American slang, a singular someone
senses.definition: an informal word for a person you are talking about
senses.definitionCN: 口语中泛指正在谈论的那个人
senses.example: You can fool the sucker who backs the other side.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以去骗那个押对方的家伙。
senses.why: American slang drifted from the cheated buyer to any anonymous man, so the word came to mean a fellow, often with contempt.
senses.whyCN: 美国俚语从被坑的买家漂移到任意一个无名男人，于是这个词用来指「那家伙」，常带轻蔑。
