intro.en: Sucker is an English noun built in late Middle English from the verb suck and the agent ending -er, so it first meant one who sucks.
intro.cn: sucker 是中古英语晚期由动词 suck 加施事后缀 -er 构成的英语本土名词，最初指「吮吸的人或物」。

items.en: A reconstructed root, written sueg-, underlies the Latin verb sugere and the English verb suck.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构词根 sueg- 是拉丁语 sugere 与英语 suck 的共同来源。

items.en: Sugere means to suck, giving suctus and the noun suctor, a sucker.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sugere 意为吮吸，衍生出 suctus 与名词 suctor（吮吸者）。

items.en: The English verb suc-an, later spelt suck, already means to draw liquid with the mouth.
items.cn: 古英语动词 sucan 已表用嘴吸液体，后拼作 suck。

items.en: Adding the agent ending -er gives sucker, a person or animal that sucks, and by the fifteenth century a young shoot.
items.cn: 加施事后缀 -er 得到 sucker，指吮吸的人或动物；十五世纪已用来指嫩芽。

items.en: Natural history writing uses sucker for the sucking organs of fish and insects.
items.cn: 十八世纪博物学著作用它指鱼类与昆虫的吸着器官。

items.en: American slang, helped by the name of a bottom-feeding fish, turns sucker into a term for an easily cheated person.
items.cn: 靠一种底栖鱼的俗名，美国俚语把 sucker 变成指「易受骗的人」的词。

note.en: The first group holds the suck family and its best known compounds; the second holds words for the things a sucker names or describes.
note.cn: 第一组是 suck 词族及其常见复合词；第二组是 sucker 所命名或描述的同类事物。

entries.definition: To draw a liquid in with the mouth, or to pull by suction.
entries.definitionCN: 用嘴吸进液体，或以吸力抽出。

entries.definition: The form used in compounds and adjectives, such as the sucking mouth of a fish.
entries.definitionCN: 用于复合词与形容词的形式，如鱼的吸吻。

entries.definition: The plural for several sucking organs or several easily fooled people.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指多个吸盘或多个轻信的人。

entries.definition: A fish that clings to larger animals with a sucking disc.
entries.definitionCN: 靠吸盘附着在大鱼身上的鱼。

entries.definition: A blow thrown at someone who is not expecting it.
entries.definitionCN: 出在别人毫无防备时的拳头。

entries.definition: A person who is tricked, often in a scheme.
entries.definitionCN: 常指被圈套欺骗的人。

entries.definition: A blunter word for someone who lacks good sense.
entries.definitionCN: 更直接地指缺少判断力的人。

entries.definition: A young stem growing from a stem or bud rather than a root.
entries.definitionCN: 从茎或芽而不是根上长出的嫩枝。

entries.definition: The desire to do something you know you should avoid.
entries.definitionCN: 想做明知不该做的事的欲望。

normalIntro.en: Link the word to its verb and to one fixed phrase, and the various meanings fall into place.
normalIntro.cn: 把词和它的动词、再加一个固定短语连起来，几个意思就都站住了。

normal.en: Sucker is suck plus -er, so think of the thing doing the sucking.
normal.cn: sucker 是 suck 加 -er，所以先想「做吮吸的那一方」。

normal.en: A sucker for the opera means someone who cannot resist it.
normal.cn: a sucker for the opera 指对歌剧毫无抵抗力的人。

normal.en: Sucker punch is not a punch about sucking; it means a blow out of the blue.
normal.cn: sucker punch 与「吸」无关，指冷不防的一拳。

normal.en: Biologists write sucker for any organ that grips by suction.
normal.cn: 生物学家用 sucker 泛指靠吸力抓住物体的器官。

normal.en: As a verb, sucker is rare outside gardening and old American speech.
normal.cn: 作动词时，sucker 主要见于园艺与旧式美国口语。

abstract.en: Watch a ring of tiny discs on an octopus arm close one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象章鱼触手上的一圈小圆盘一个接一个合拢。

abstract.en: See a green shoot pushing straight up beside a tree trunk.
abstract.cn: 看到一株绿芽从树干旁边直直冒出来。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber pad pressed to a wet floor and refusing to lift.
abstract.cn: 想象一块橡胶垫压上湿地面，怎么也拔不起来。

examples.en: A clever con artist can always find a sucker.
examples.cn: 老练的骗子总能找到上钩的傻瓜。

examples.en: The plant sends out suckers from its roots every spring.
examples.cn: 这种植物每年春天都从根上长出根出条。

examples.en: The lampreys use the suckers around their mouths to cling to rocks.
examples.cn: 七鳃鳗用嘴周的吸盘附着在岩石上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨克」——想着章鱼的吸盘「嗦」地一声吸住玻璃；sucker 就是吸盘，也可以比喻张嘴就信、被人吸走钱的人。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语动词 suck（吮吸，古英语 sucan）＋ 施事后缀 -er → sucker（吮吸的人或物）→「吸盘、根出条、易受骗的人、底栖鱼」；一般认为更早与拉丁语 sugere（吮吸）同源于重构词根 sueg-。

sensesIntro.en: Sucker begins with the action of sucking: the organ that sucks, the shoot that sucks food from its parent, and the person who sucks in lies lead from one picture of a mouth that grips.
sensesIntro.cn: sucker 从「吸」这个动作出发：做吸的器官、吮吸母株养分的根出条、把谎话一吸而尽的轻信者，都源自同一幅「会咬住的嘴」的画面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of small cups that grips the moment it touches glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈小杯状物一碰到玻璃就牢牢吸住。

branches.en: The organ and the pump both grip by removing pressure.
branches.cn: 器官与吸泵都靠降低压力来吸住。

branches.en: The fool believes too easily, and the word also names the person you are talking about.
branches.cn: 轻信者太容易上当，这个词也用来指谈话中的那个人。

branches.en: The root shoot pulls food as if sucking it from the parent.
branches.cn: 根出条像吮吸母株一样吸取养分。

branches.en: The shoe pad and the fish are both named for their sucking grip.
branches.cn: 鞋底防滑片与底栖鱼都因吸住的样子得名。

branches.en: A mouth that grips and a mind that swallows lies share the same image.
branches.cn: 会咬住的嘴与照单全收谎言的头脑共用同一画面。

intro.en: Most of this word family is native English: the verb suck plus endings and compounds, with one Latin relative in sugere.
intro.cn: 这个词族大部分是英语本土成分：动词 suck 加词尾、构复合词，另有一个拉丁亲戚 sugere。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb sugere means to suck and yields suctus, a sucking, and suckle words appear through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 sugere 意为吮吸，衍生出 suctus（吮吸），而「喂奶」一类词经法语传入英语。

items.example: The verb suck is the whole stem of the family.
items.exampleCN: 动词 suck 是整个词族的词干。

items.meaning: one who or that which does
items.example: The suffix -er turns the verb into the doer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把动词变成做动作的一方。

items.example: Sucker first means one who sucks.
items.exampleCN: sucker 最初指吮吸的人或物。

items.example: The plural adds a plain s.
items.exampleCN: 复数只加一个 s。

items.example: The ending -ing gives sucking.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 sucking。

items.example: The ending -ling marks a small creature.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ling 标出小家伙。

items.meaning: a fish that clings by a disc
items.example: The compound joins sucker to fish.
items.exampleCN: 复合词把 sucker 与 fish 连起来。

items.example: The phrase works as one unit of meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语整体表示一个意思。

items.example: Suckerfish carries the ending -ish.
items.exampleCN: suckerfish 末尾带 -ish。

definition_zh: 吸；抽吸；吸力；吸吮
definition_en: the act of removing air or liquid from a space so that something is pulled in or held
core_image: 杯中的空气被抽走，水边的小纸片被吸进杯口
scene: 水管堵住时，师傅用一只橡胶吸盘上下抽动。When the pipe was blocked, the plumber used a rubber plunger to create suction and pull the waste away.
sceneCN: 这里 suction 是「抽吸」（第 1 个义项：抽走空气或液体形成吸力的过程）；句意：水管堵住时，师傅用一只橡胶吸盘上下抽动，制造抽吸力把污物拉走。

pos.zh: 吸力的；用于抽吸的（见于复合词）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词根加 -al 构成，义为「适于吸吮的」，多用于动物学的吸盘类生物
由简单词加 -al 构成，义为「与抽吸相关的」，属技术性用语
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「抽吸过程」，常见于医疗护理

senses.title: The process of drawing air or liquid inward
senses.definition: the force created when air or liquid is removed from a space, so that other matter is pulled into it
senses.definitionCN: 从某处抽走空气或液体后形成的力量，把其他物质拉进去
senses.example: The nurse used suction to clear the wound.
senses.exampleCN: 护士用抽吸的方法清理伤口。
senses.why: Low pressure is the heart of the image: when a space loses air, the surrounding matter rushes in.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是压强差：一个空间失去空气后，周围的东西就被压进去，这正是「吸」的物理起点。

senses.title: A device that works by suction
senses.definition: an apparatus such as a pump or a tube that moves air, liquid, or waste by creating low pressure
senses.definitionCN: 通过制造低压来移动空气、液体或污物的装置，如泵或管子
senses.example: The suction unit was wheeled into the operating room.
senses.exampleCN: 抽吸设备被推入了手术室。
senses.why: Once people made the force useful, they built machines around it, so the word often names the equipment itself.
senses.whyCN: 人们一旦把这种力变成可用的工具，就会用同一个词指称机器，于是「抽吸」抽象为「抽吸装置」。

senses.title: The holding force of a cup or pad
senses.definition: the power by which a hollow object with its air removed sticks firmly to a flat surface
senses.definitionCN: 把内部空气排空的中空物体牢牢贴住平面的力量
senses.example: The mirror stays on the tiles by suction alone.
senses.exampleCN: 这面镜子仅凭吸力就固定在瓷砖上。
senses.why: From pulling matter inward to holding an object on a wall, the same low pressure explains why a cup clings.
senses.whyCN: 从把东西吸进来，到让一杯子挂在墙上，背后的低压原理是同一个，所以「吸力」自然长出了「吸附力」这层意思。

senses.title: The movement of a baby or animal drawing milk
senses.definition: the mouth movement by which an infant or young animal draws milk from its mother
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿或幼兽把乳汁从母体吸出的口部动作
senses.example: Feeding depends on a strong suction reflex in the newborn.
senses.exampleCN: 喂养依靠新生儿强有力的吸吮反射。
senses.why: The earliest and most intimate case of drawing inward is nursing, a mouth creating a vacuum of its own.
senses.whyCN: 最贴近身体的吸水动作就是吃奶：嘴自己制造真空，所以把「抽吸」往身体方向推一步就得到了「吸吮」。

senses.title: Hollow objects cleaned by drawing air or liquid
senses.definition: the practice of clearing a hollow space or a surface by drawing away fluid and debris with a vacuum
senses.definitionCN: 用真空抽走液体和杂物，以清洁中空空间或表面的做法
senses.example: Regular suction keeps the drain free of blockages.
senses.exampleCN: 定期抽吸能让下水道保持畅通。
senses.why: Applied to pipes, wounds, and chimneys, the force becomes a maintenance routine whose name is the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 当这种力用在管道、伤口和烟囱上，就变成一种日常维护手段，而这一手段只在「抽吸」这个词里才最准确。

senses.title: The pull of moving air or water on things nearby
senses.definition: the drawing of nearby objects into a stream of fast moving air or water
senses.definitionCN: 快速流动的空气或水流把附近的物体拉进流中
senses.example: The boat was caught in the suction of the propellers.
senses.exampleCN: 小船被螺旋桨的吸卷力带住了。
senses.why: Physics shows that a fast moving fluid leaves a pocket of low pressure behind it, and anything close is drawn in.
senses.whyCN: 快速流动的流体身后会留下低压区，靠近的东西就被卷进去，所以「抽吸」也能描述航船、引擎周围的「吸卷」。

senses.title: Pressure difference as a technical cause
senses.definition: the effect of a pressure difference that moves or holds matter, as measured or designed in engineering
senses.definitionCN: 压强差带来的移动或固定物质的效果，在工程中被测量和设计
senses.example: The factory uses suction to lift heavy glass panels.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂用抽吸的方式吊起沉重的玻璃板。
senses.why: In technical writing the word can name the physical effect itself, which is measured in units of pressure.
senses.whyCN: 在技术文本里，这个词可以直接指物理效果本身，它以压强作为计量单位，于是义项抽象为「吸力作用」。

senses.title: A clinging hold in a figurative sense
senses.definition: the quality of something that grips a person or group so strongly that they seem stuck to it
senses.definitionCN: 某事物对人牢牢攫住、仿佛贴住不放的性质
senses.example: Debt has a suction effect on the family budget.
senses.exampleCN: 债务对家庭预算有吸附效应。
senses.why: From a cup on a wall to a habit on a person, the metaphor keeps the same picture of being held by a pulling force.
senses.whyCN: 从墙上的吸盘引申到人身上的习惯，比喻保留了同一个画面：被一股拉力攫住，无从脱身。

intro.en: Suction travels from Latin sugere, to suck, through the Late Latin noun suctio.
intro.cn: suction 上溯拉丁语 sugere（吸吮），经由晚期拉丁语名词 suctio 进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root partly built on the syllable su suggests the sucking sound.
items.cn: 重构词根以 su 音节为核心，一般认为模仿吸吮的声音（重构形式）。

items.en: The verb sugere means to suck, and gives the past participle suctus.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 sugere 意为吸吮，其过去分词为 suctus。

items.en: The noun suctio names the act of sucking.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语名词 suctio 意为吸吮的动作。

items.en: The noun enters the learned vocabulary of physics and medicine.
items.cn: 进入物理学与医学的学术词汇，指真空造成的吸取。

items.en: English borrows the noun and extends it to pumps and cups.
items.cn: 英语借入该名词，并推广到泵与吸盘等器械。

items.en: Modern use covers medical, industrial, and figurative senses.
items.cn: 现代用法覆盖医疗、工业与比喻义项。

note.en: Suction sits between the everyday verb suck and noun groups such as vacuum and siphon.
note.cn: suction 夹在日常动词 suck 与 vacuum、siphon 等名词之间，名词性更强。

entries.definition: to draw liquid or air into the mouth or a device
entries.definitionCN: 吸；吮；抽吸

entries.definition: adapted for sucking, as in the mouthparts of some insects
entries.definitionCN: 适于吸吮的（如某些昆虫的口器）

entries.definition: sugar, from the Latin word for juice
entries.definitionCN: 蔗糖，来自拉丁语表中汁液的词，与吸吮同源

entries.definition: to feed a baby or young animal from the breast
entries.definitionCN: 哺乳；给婴儿或幼兽喂奶

entries.definition: a space with no matter, or a machine that creates one
entries.definitionCN: 真空；吸尘器（只是义场相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a tube that carries liquid upward over a higher point
entries.definitionCN: 虹吸管（只是义场相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a machine that moves liquid or gas
entries.definitionCN: 泵；水泵

normalIntro.en: Suction is pressure at work: a space loses air, and the world presses in.
normalIntro.cn: suction 是压强在工作：空间失去空气，周围世界就压进来。

normal.en: Suction is the noun, suck is the everyday verb.
normal.cn: suction 是名词，suck 是日常动词，两者同源。

normal.en: A suction pump moves water by lowering the pressure inside.
normal.cn: 抽吸泵靠降低内部压强来移动水。

normal.en: A suction cup holds a mirror on glass for years.
normal.cn: 吸盘能在玻璃上把镜子固定许多年。

normal.en: In medicine, suction clears the airway before surgery.
normal.cn: 医学上，抽吸常用于术前清理气道。

normal.en: Compare vacuum, which names the empty space itself.
normal.cn: 对比 vacuum：那里强调的是「真空」这个空间本身。

abstract.en: Picture a straw pulling the last juice from a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象用吸管吸走杯底最后一滴果汁。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand pressing a rubber pad flat on a window.
abstract.cn: 想象用手把一块橡胶垫压平在窗玻璃上。

abstract.en: Think of a whirlpool dragging leaves toward its centre.
abstract.cn: 想象漩涡把落叶拖向中心。

examples.en: The suction of the vacuum cleaner picked up every crumb.
examples.cn: 吸尘器的吸力把每一粒碎屑都吸走了。

examples.en: Surgeons rely on suction to keep the wound clear.
examples.cn: 外科医生依靠抽吸来保持创面清晰。

examples.en: The suction cup failed on the wet tiles.
examples.cn: 吸盘在湿瓷砖上失去了吸力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨克申」——听起来像「萨克斯里吸一口气」，把「吸」的动作和声音连在一起；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sugere（吸吮）→ 过去分词 suctus → 晚期拉丁语 suctio（吸吮）→ 英语 suction，核心义「把东西吸进来」。

sensesIntro.en: Suction begins as a physical drawing of air or liquid, then names devices, nursing, cleaning, propellers, engineered pressure, and finally a clinging grip in metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: suction 从物理上的「抽走空气或液体」出发，依次扩展到器械、哺乳、清理、吸卷、工程压强，最后延伸到比喻中的「牢牢吸附」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air removed from a cup so that whatever is near is pulled in.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯中空气被抽走，附近的东西被拉进去。

branches.en: The basic act of drawing in and its use for cleaning belong together.
branches.cn: 基本的抽吸动作与用于清理的抽吸属于同一层。

branches.en: Devices and engineered pressure are the technical side.
branches.cn: 器械与经过设计的压强属于技术一面。

branches.en: A cup on a wall and a habit on a person share the clinging image.
branches.cn: 墙上的吸盘与人身上的习惯共享「贴住不放」的意象。

branches.en: Nursing is the most bodily form of drawing inward.
branches.cn: 哺乳是把东西吸进身体最直接的形式。

branches.en: Propellers and rapids show the force acting on nearby objects.
branches.cn: 螺旋桨与急流展示了这种力作用于附近物体。

intro.en: Suction is built from the Latin verb sugere plus the abstract suffix -tion.
intro.cn: suction 由拉丁动词 sugere 加抽象名词后缀 -tion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sugere, to suck, shortens to suct- before the noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sugere（吸吮）在名词词尾前缩为 suct-。

items.example: Sugere gives the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: sugere 提供整个词族的词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -tion turns an act into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 把动作变成名词。

items.example: Suction names the act itself.
items.exampleCN: suction 指动作本身。

items.meaning: to draw liquid into the mouth
items.example: Suck is the everyday verb of the same root.
items.exampleCN: suck 是同根最日常的动词。

items.meaning: a rubber cup that sticks by suction
items.meaningCN: 靠吸力贴住的橡胶吸盘
items.example: A suction cup holds the soap dish.
items.exampleCN: 吸盘托住了肥皂盒。

items.meaning: a pump driven by pressure difference
items.example: The suction pump emptied the tank.
items.exampleCN: 抽吸泵抽空了水箱。

items.example: The wound was suctioned twice.
items.exampleCN: 伤口被抽吸清理了两次。

items.meaning: one that does, or relating to
items.meaningCN: 表示施动者或相关的后缀
items.example: The suffix -or appears in related technical words.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 见于相关的技术词。

items.example: Suckle repeats the mouth image of the root.
items.exampleCN: suckle 重复了词根中的口部意象。

items.example: Suctorial describes insect mouthparts.
items.exampleCN: suctorial 描述昆虫的口器。

definition_zh: 起诉；控告；请求；追求
definition_en: to take legal action against someone, or formally to ask for something
core_image: 一个人举着一叠文件，追着另一个人一直追到衙门前
scene: 租客把房东告上了法庭。After the landlord refused to return the deposit, the tenant decided to sue him in court.
sceneCN: 这里 sue 是「起诉」（第 1 个义项：向法院提出诉讼，要求对方承担法律责任）；句意：房东拒绝退还押金后，租客决定向法院起诉他。

collocations.phrase: sue someone for breach of contract

derivatives.zh: 由同源名词分化而来，义为「诉讼；官司」，也指「一套衣服」
由同源词承接「追随、符合」之义，义为「适合；相称」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「起诉行为」，法律文本中可见

senses.title: To bring a legal case against someone
senses.definition: to start a legal case against a person or an organization, especially to claim money or a right
senses.definitionCN: 对个人或机构提起诉讼，尤其为了索要款项或主张权利
senses.example: The residents sued the factory over the polluted river.
senses.exampleCN: 居民因河流被污染而起诉这家工厂。
senses.why: The old sense of following was legalized: a plaintiff follows a defendant into court and demands a hearing.
senses.whyCN: 「跟随」的旧义走上法庭就成了「起诉」：原告一路追着被告进法院，要求给对方一个裁判。

senses.title: To make a formal request to an authority
senses.definition: to make a formal and humble request to a person or body that has the power to grant it
senses.definitionCN: 向有权准许的人或机构正式而谦恭地请求
senses.example: The villagers sued the king for relief after the floods.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，村民们向国王请求救济。
senses.why: To follow someone is also to approach them with a plea, and this courtly sense survived in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 跟随某人也是走到他面前开口请托，这一宫廷色彩的含义在正式文书中保留了下来。

senses.title: To ask courts for an official decision by petition
senses.definition: to present a petition or application to a court or a law court asking for a specific order
senses.definitionCN: 向法院或法庭提交申请书，请求作出特定裁定
senses.example: She sued for custody of the two children.
senses.exampleCN: 她为两个孩子的监护权提起了诉讼。
senses.why: Between a plea and a lawsuit there is a petition, which asks the court itself to decide a matter.
senses.whyCN: 在恳求与诉讼之间是「诉请」：它请求的不是对方，而是法院本身作出裁定。

senses.title: To seek something by persistent action
senses.definition: to pursue a goal such as peace, justice, or help through steady effort
senses.definitionCN: 通过持续努力去追求和平、正义或帮助等目标
senses.example: Both sides sent envoys to sue for peace.
senses.exampleCN: 双方都派使者去求和。
senses.why: The following image widens from legal suits to any goal that a person chases on foot and on paper.
senses.whyCN: 「跟随」的意象从法律诉讼扩大到任何目标：人用脚步和文书一路去追。

senses.title: To take someone to court in everyday speech
senses.definition: used in everyday speech for the act of threatening or starting litigation against a person
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中指威胁或启动对某人的法律诉讼
senses.example: He says he will sue anyone who copies his design.
senses.exampleCN: 他说谁抄他的设计他就告谁。
senses.why: Modern speech has made the verb a quick, blunt verb of action, often used in warnings.
senses.whyCN: 现代口语把这个动词变成一个干脆的行动词，常出现在警告里，说出口就是施压。

senses.title: The noun form for a legal action
senses.definition: a less common noun use meaning a legal action or the right to bring one
senses.definitionCN: 较少见的名词用法，指一次诉讼或提起诉讼的权利
senses.example: The lease gives the tenant a right of sue in the local court.
senses.exampleCN: 租约赋予租客在当地法院提起诉讼的权利。
senses.why: Legal Latin used both a verb and a noun, and English keeps a rare noun trace in legal phrases.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语里动词与名词并存，英语在部分法律短语中留下稀有的名词痕迹。

intro.en: Sue descends from Latin sequi, to follow, through the Old French verb sivre and its legal noun suite.
intro.cn: sue 源出拉丁语 sequi（跟随），经古法语动词 sivre 及法律名词 suite 进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root means to follow, and gives Latin sequi.
items.cn: 重构词根意为跟随，由此派生拉丁语 sequi（重构形式）。

items.en: Sequi means to follow; secta and sectare add a way of life or pursuit.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随；secta 与 sectare 则增添「道路」「追逐」的意义。

items.en: Sivre means to follow, and the legal noun suite means a following or a suit.
items.cn: 古法语 sivre 意为跟随，法律名词 suite 指追随者或诉讼。

items.en: Legal French suer passes into court practice in England.
items.cn: 法律法语 suer 进入英格兰的法庭实务。

items.en: Sewen and suen mean to follow, to beg, and to bring an action.
items.cn: 中古英语 sewen、suen 兼有跟随、恳求与提起诉讼之义。

items.en: The chasing sense fades and the legal sense becomes standard.
items.cn: 「追赶」义弱化，法律义成为标准用法。

note.en: Sue is a legal verb of following, close to pursue, prosecute, and the everyday words accuse and charge.
note.cn: sue 是「跟随」演变来的法律动词，与 pursue、prosecute 形近，也与 accuse、charge 义近。

entries.definition: to follow someone in order to catch them
entries.definitionCN: 追赶；追捕；追求

entries.definition: to bring a criminal charge against someone in court
entries.definitionCN: 提起公诉；检控

entries.definition: a legal case, or a set of matching clothes
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼；一套衣服（与 sue 同源）

entries.definition: a set of connected rooms or pieces
entries.definitionCN: 套房；一套（同源，注意拼写不同）

entries.definition: to say that someone has done something wrong
entries.definitionCN: 指控；指责（不一定是法律行为）

entries.definition: to formally accuse someone of a crime
entries.definitionCN: 正式控告某人犯罪

entries.definition: to take part in a lawsuit
entries.definitionCN: 打官司；进行诉讼

normalIntro.en: Sue is a legal mask on the shared idea of following: pursue someone until a court hears the case.
normalIntro.cn: sue 是「跟随」的法律面具：一路追着某人，直到法院受理。

normal.en: Sue and suit come from the same Old French word.
normal.cn: sue 与 suit 来自同一个古法语词。

normal.en: To sue for divorce means to ask a court to end a marriage.
normal.cn: sue for divorce 指请求法院解除婚姻。

normal.en: To sue someone for damages is to claim money in court.
normal.cn: sue someone for damages 指在法院索要赔款。

normal.en: Compare pursue: pursue is to chase, sue is to chase into court.
normal.cn: 对比 pursue：pursue 是追赶，sue 是追进法院。

normal.en: Lawyers call the person who sues the plaintiff.
normal.cn: 律师把提起诉讼的人称作 plaintiff。

abstract.en: Picture someone holding a folder high and walking fast to a courthouse.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人高举文件夹匆忙走向法院。

abstract.en: Imagine a dotted line of footprints from a house to a judge door.
abstract.cn: 想象一串脚印从一间屋子一直连到法官门口。

abstract.en: Think of a knock that turns into a formal petition.
abstract.cn: 想象一声敲门慢慢变成一份正式诉状。

examples.en: The company sued its former partner for breach of contract.
examples.cn: 这家公司以违约为由起诉了前合伙人。

examples.en: You cannot sue for damages without proof.
examples.cn: 没有证据就无法起诉索赔。

examples.en: The writers are suing the website over unpaid royalties.
examples.cn: 这些作家正因未付版税起诉该网站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「苏」——像讨债的人上门说「输赢要说法」，一口咬定就要上法院；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sequi（跟随）→ 古法语 sivre（跟随）与 suite（诉讼）→ 中古英语 suen → 英语 sue，核心义由「追赶」转为「追诉」。

sensesIntro.en: Sue starts from following: first into court as a lawsuit, then as a formal request, a petition to a court, a steady pursuit, and finally loose everyday and rare noun uses.
sensesIntro.cn: sue 由「跟随」出发：先跟到法院成为诉讼，再跟出正式请求、向法院诉请、持续谋求，最后是口语化的「告人」与罕见的名词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person follows another all the way to the courthouse door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人一路跟着另一个人走进法院大门。

branches.en: The full lawsuit and its everyday spoken form belong together.
branches.cn: 完整的诉讼与它的口语说法属于同一条支线。

branches.en: Formal pleas and steady pursuit keep the older sense of asking.
branches.cn: 正式恳求与持续谋求保留了「请求」的旧义。

branches.en: A petition asks the court itself to decide.
branches.cn: 诉请是请求法院本身来裁决。

branches.en: Both a suit and a petition begin with a written filing.
branches.cn: 诉讼与诉请都以书面提交为起点。

branches.en: The rare noun use is the legal trace of the same word.
branches.cn: 罕见的名词用法是同一个词留下的法律痕迹。

intro.en: Sue is a stripped down French verb whose relatives in Latin begin with sequ- or sect-.
intro.cn: sue 是被削减到极简的法语动词，其拉丁亲属以 sequ- 或 sect- 开头。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi, to follow, gives pursue, suite, and the whole set of following words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sequi（跟随）衍生出 pursue、suite 等整组同族词。

items.example: Sequi gives the root of a large family of words.
items.exampleCN: sequi 提供这一大族词的词根。

items.example: Sue is the reduced French form.
items.exampleCN: sue 是削减后的法语形式。

items.example: The prefix pur- plus follow makes pursue.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pur- 加跟随构成 pursue。

items.meaning: to follow in order to catch
items.example: Pursue keeps the literal chasing.
items.exampleCN: pursue 保留了字面的追赶。

items.example: The prefix pro- plus follow makes prosecute.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 加跟随构成 prosecute。

items.example: Prosecute is the criminal cousin of sue.
items.exampleCN: prosecute 是 sue 的刑事近亲。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms prosecution.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 构成 prosecution。

items.example: Suite became a set of rooms.
items.exampleCN: suite 后来指一套房间。

items.meaning: one who follows in order to court
items.example: Suitor is the person who follows.
items.exampleCN: suitor 指跟随的那一方。

items.example: The prefix sub- plus follow makes subsequent.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 加跟随构成 subsequent。

latinEntries.meaning: a way of life, a following

definition_zh: 足够；满足需要；使满足
definition_en: to be enough for a particular purpose, or to satisfy a need
core_image: 一只碗里的水刚好拍到碗口，再多一滴就会溢出
scene: 背包里只剩两瓶水，够大家喝完今天这段路了。Two bottles of water will suffice for the rest of the walk.
sceneCN: 这里 suffice 是「足够」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度正好满足需要，不必再多）；句意：剩下的这段路，两瓶水就够了。

pos.zh: （suffice it to say 等固定表达中）只需说

collocations.zh: 只要说……就够了（固定表达）
自给自足；自足（古雅固定表达）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ent 构成，义为「足够的；充分的」
由形容词加 -cy 构成，义为「充足；足量」
由否定前缀 in- 加 sufficient 构成，义为「不足的」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「足够地」
动词第三人称单数形式，义为「足够」

senses.title: To be enough for a purpose
senses.definition: to be as much as is needed for a particular aim, so that nothing more is required
senses.definitionCN: 达到某个目标所需的量，不必再增加
senses.example: A short note will suffice for the record.
senses.exampleCN: 记录用一张便条就够了。
senses.why: The Latin source is sufficere, to supply or put under, which pictures a supply placed beneath a need until it is met.
senses.whyCN: 词源 sufficere 意为「供给、垫在下面」，把供给垫在需要之下直到刚好填满，这就是「足够」的画面。

senses.title: To satisfy a need or a request
senses.definition: to meet the demands of a person or a situation so that they are satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 满足某人的要求或某种情形的需要，使其得到满足
senses.example: One example will suffice to prove the point.
senses.exampleCN: 一个例子就足以证明这一点。
senses.why: If a supply placed beneath a need fills it, the supply also satisfies the one who needed it.
senses.whyCN: 既然供给垫在需要下面把空当填满，它同时也就让对方「满足了」，所以从「够」自然过渡到「满足」。

senses.title: In the fixed phrase suffice it to say
senses.definition: used in the set phrase suffice it to say to mean that a short statement is enough
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定表达 suffice it to say，意为说一句话就已足够
senses.example: Suffice it to say that the meeting ended badly.
senses.exampleCN: 只说一句就够了：会开得很不愉快。
senses.why: The verb is placed in an old subjunctive frame, so the claim that a word is enough becomes a rhetorical formula.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词被放进古老的虚拟句式里，「一句话就够了」的说法就成了修辞套语。

senses.title: Barely enough, with nothing to spare
senses.definition: to be just enough, so that there is very little or nothing left over
senses.definitionCN: 刚好够用，几乎没有剩余
senses.example: The little money they had sufficed to buy bread only.
senses.exampleCN: 他们仅有的一点钱只够买面包。
senses.why: Take the image literally: the bowl is filled to the brim, and a single drop would overflow.
senses.whyCN: 把画面想得更具体：碗里刚好满到边沿，再一滴就溢出来，这就是「勉强够」。

senses.title: To prove adequate in a test or argument
senses.definition: to be strong enough as evidence or argument to support a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 作为证据或理由足够有力，能够支撑一个结论
senses.example: Such evidence does not suffice to convict the man.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的证据不足以给这个人定罪。
senses.why: Legal and logical use asks whether the material placed under a claim is enough to hold it up.
senses.whyCN: 法律与逻辑上的用法问的是：垫在某个论断底下的材料，够不够把它撑住。

senses.title: Self sufficiency as a way of life
senses.definition: used of a person or a household that supplies its own needs without outside help
senses.definitionCN: 指个人或家庭无需外援就能供给自己所需
senses.example: The village hopes to suffice for itself within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子希望十年内能够自给自足。
senses.why: When the thing that fills the need is a person or a community, the verb turns into a statement about independence.
senses.whyCN: 当填满需要的是一个人或一个村落时，这个动词就变成了关于独立的陈述。

intro.en: Suffice comes from Latin sufficere, to supply or be adequate, built from sub-, under, and facere, to make.
intro.cn: suffice 来自拉丁语 sufficere（供给、足够），由 sub-（在下面）与 facere（做、使）构成。

items.en: The root dhe means to put or to set, and gives Latin facere.
items.cn: 重构词根 dhe 意为放置、设置，衍生拉丁语 facere（做）（重构形式）。

items.en: Facere means to make, and sufficere means to put beneath, then to supply.
items.cn: facere 意为做；sufficere 意为垫在下面，后引申为供给。

items.en: Sufficere also means to be enough, as of resources placed under a demand.
items.cn: sufficere 进一步表示足够，好像资源被垫在需求之下。

items.en: Sofire and suffire carry the sense of being enough.
items.cn: 古法语 sofire、suffire 表示足够。

items.en: Suffisen means to be enough or to supply what is needed.
items.cn: 中古英语 suffisen 意为足够或供给所需。

items.en: The verb becomes formal, and adjectives such as sufficient take over everyday use.
items.cn: 这个动词变得正式，日常中更多用 sufficient 等形容词。

note.en: Suffice is the formal verb behind sufficient; it neighbours enough and satisfy in meaning and suffuse in shape.
note.cn: suffice 是 sufficient 背后的正式动词，意义上邻近 enough、satisfy，外形上易与 suffuse 混淆。

entries.definitionCN: 足够的；充分的

entries.definition: the state of being enough
entries.definitionCN: 充足；足量

entries.definition: to spread over a surface as light or colour
entries.definitionCN: 弥漫；布满（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自 fundere 倾倒）

entries.definition: not enough
entries.definitionCN: 不足的

entries.definition: as much as is needed
entries.definitionCN: 足够的（日常用语，可作形容词、副词）

entries.definition: good enough in quantity or quality
entries.definitionCN: 足够的；胜任的

entries.definition: to meet the needs or wishes of someone
entries.definitionCN: 使满意；满足

normalIntro.en: Suffice is a supply tucked under a need: just enough, no overflow.
normalIntro.cn: suffice 是塞在需要底下的一份供给：刚刚好，不多溢。

normal.en: Suffice is the verb, sufficient and sufficiency are its noun and adjective.
normal.cn: suffice 是动词，sufficient 与 sufficiency 是同根形容词与名词。

normal.en: Suffice for means to be enough for a need.
normal.cn: suffice for 表示对某种需要足够。

normal.en: Suffice it to say introduces a brief summary.
normal.cn: suffice it to say 用来引出简短的总结。

normal.en: The prefix in- makes insufficient, which means not enough.
normal.cn: 加上前缀 in- 就是 insufficient，意为不足。

normal.en: The Latin parts are sub-, under, and facere, to make.
normal.cn: 拉丁语构件是 sub-（在下）与 facere（做）。

abstract.en: Picture a cup filled exactly to the rim.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子正好满到杯口。

abstract.en: Imagine a single cushion placed exactly under a heavy box.
abstract.cn: 想象一只垫子正好垫在重箱子底下。

abstract.en: Think of a small coin dropped into a slot that is just the right size.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小硬币落进大小刚好的投币口。

examples.en: A brief email will suffice; there is no need for a long report.
examples.cn: 一封简短的邮件就够了，不必写长篇报告。

examples.en: Her salary suffices to cover rent and food.
examples.cn: 她的工资足以支付房租和饭钱。

examples.en: Suffice it to say that we were late.
examples.cn: 只说一句就够了：我们迟到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「少放一勺」——少放一勺也「足够」了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ facere（做、使）→ sufficere（垫在下面；供给；足够）→ 古法语 suffire → 中古英语 suffisen → 现代英语 suffice，核心义「供给正好填满需要」。

sensesIntro.en: Suffice moves from being enough for a purpose, to satisfying a person, to the fixed phrase, to bare adequacy, to proof, and finally to a community supplying itself.
sensesIntro.cn: suffice 由「够某个目标用」，到「使某人满足」，再到固定表达、刚好够用、证据成立，最后到人自给自足。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a supply laid beneath a need until it is exactly full.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份供给垫在需要底下，恰好填满。

branches.en: Enough and barely enough are the same picture at slightly different levels.
branches.cn: 「够」与「勉强够」是同一画面在水量高低上的差别。

branches.en: Satisfying a person and supporting a claim are both forms of adequacy.
branches.cn: 满足一个人与支撑一个论断都是「足以」的不同对象。

branches.en: The fixed phrase freezes the idea of a word being enough.
branches.cn: 固定表达把「一句话就够了」冻结成套语。

branches.en: When the supplier is the needy one, enough becomes self sufficiency.
branches.cn: 当供给者就是需要者时，「足够」就变成「自给自足」。

branches.en: Satisfaction is the emotional result of a need being filled.
branches.cn: 满足感是需要被填满后产生的结果。

intro.en: Suffice is a Latin compound of a prefix and the root fac-, carried into English through French.
intro.cn: suffice 是拉丁语中「前缀加 fac- 词根」的复合词，经商法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin sufficere joins sub-, under, with facere, to make, so the family shares the make root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sufficere 由 sub-（在下）与 facere（做）结合，整族词都带着「做」的词根。

items.example: The prefix sub- gives the image of putting under.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 提供「垫在下面」的画面。

items.example: Facere gives the make root of the family.
items.exampleCN: facere 提供本族「做」的词根。

items.example: Suffice is the verb in modern use.
items.exampleCN: suffice 是现代的动词形式。

items.meaningCN: 处于某种状态的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ent forms sufficient.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 构成 sufficient。

items.example: Sufficient replaces the verb in everyday sentences.
items.exampleCN: 日常句中常用 sufficient 取代动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -cy forms sufficiency.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 构成 sufficiency。

items.example: The prefix in- forms insufficient.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 insufficient。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms sufficiently.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 sufficiently。

items.meaningCN: 容易的；轻率的（同出 facere）
items.example: Facile comes from the same make root.
items.exampleCN: facile 同出「做」这个词根。

items.example: Fiction keeps the sense of something made.
items.exampleCN: fiction 保留「被做出来」的含义。

latinEntries.meaning: to put under, to supply, to be enough

definition_zh: 后缀；词尾；附加在词后的成分；加后缀
definition_en: a letter or group of letters added to the end of a word to change its meaning or grammar, or to add such an ending
core_image: 一句话讲完，句尾再钉上一个小小的尾巴，把意思拧个方向
scene: 老师先写下动词，又在词尾添上一个小尾巴，把它变成表示人的名词。The teacher wrote the verb on the board and then added a suffix to turn it into a noun for a person.
sceneCN: 这里 suffix 是「后缀」（第 1 个义项：加在词尾以改变词义或词性的成分）；句意：老师先写下动词，又在词尾添上一个小尾巴，把它变成表示人的名词。

derivatives.zh: 由 -ation 构成，义为「加后缀的过程」
由 -ed 构成，义为「带后缀的」
由 -al 与 -ly 逐层构成，义为「以后缀方式地」，极为罕见

senses.title: A letter group fastened to the end of a word
senses.definition: a letter or letters added to the end of a word or stem, used to form a new word or word form
senses.definitionCN: 加在词或词干末尾的一个或几个字母，用来构成新词或新的词形
senses.example: The suffix -able turns verbs like read into adjectives.
senses.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把 read 这类动词变成形容词。
senses.why: Latin suffigere means to fasten underneath or on, and a suffix is a piece fastened onto the end of a completed word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 suffigere 意为「在下面或上面固定」，而后缀就是固定在已完成词语末尾的一小块成分。

senses.title: An ending that marks grammar
senses.definition: an inflectional ending that marks tense, number, case, or person without making a new word
senses.definitionCN: 只标记时态、数、格或人称而不造新词的屈折词尾
senses.example: The past tense suffix -ed changes the form of the verb.
senses.exampleCN: 过去时后缀 -ed 改变动词的形式。
senses.why: Because every piece fixed to the end is called a suffix, this role sits naturally in the same ending position as the word-forming sense.
senses.whyCN: 因为凡固定在词尾的成分统称后缀，这个角色自然落在与构词义相同的末尾位置上。

senses.title: A word so formed
senses.definition: a word that has been formed by adding such an ending
senses.definitionCN: 通过添加这类词尾而形成的词
senses.example: Words with the suffix -tion often name a process.
senses.exampleCN: 带后缀 -tion 的词往往表示一个过程。
senses.why: When linguists say a word takes a suffix, they often turn around and call the resulting word a suffix form.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家说某词带后缀时，常常反过来把由此形成的词称作带后缀的形式。

senses.title: A something added on afterwards
senses.titleCN: 附加物；附在后面的成分
senses.definition: any element, remark, or number tacked onto the end of an ordered series
senses.definitionCN: 任何加在序列末尾的成分、语句或数字
senses.example: The edition number was printed as a suffix after the title.
senses.exampleCN: 版次号作为后缀印在标题之后。
senses.why: The plain idea of fastening something onto an end extends easily from letters to numbers and to remarks.
senses.whyCN: 把某物固定在末尾的朴素想法，很容易从字母扩展到数字和话语上。

senses.title: To fasten (an ending) on
senses.definition: to add a letter or letters to the end of a word or stem
senses.definitionCN: 在词或词干的末尾加上字母
senses.example: The program suffixes every output file with a date code.
senses.exampleCN: 程序给每个输出文件加上日期编码作后缀。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: to suffix something is to do the fastening that the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词与名词互为表里：给某物加后缀，就是执行名词所命名的那个固定动作。

intro.en: Suffix is a Latin formation: sub-, meaning under, plus figere, meaning to fasten, so the word itself ends with a bit of grammar fastened on.
intro.cn: suffix 是拉丁语构成：sub- 意为「在下面」，figere 意为「固定」，所以这个词本身就带着一个加上去的词尾。

items.en: Sub means under, and figere means to fasten or fix.
items.cn: sub 意为在下，figere 意为固定。

items.en: Suffigere means to fasten on underneath or upon.
items.cn: suffigere 意为固定在下或固定在上面。

items.en: Suffixum is a participle used as a noun for something fastened on at the end.
items.cn: suffixum 是分词作名词，指固定在末尾之物。

items.en: Grammarians revive the noun suffixum for an element put after a stem.
items.cn: 语法学家复活名词 suffixum，指加在词干后的成分。

items.en: English suffix appears in its modern technical sense.
items.cn: 英语 suffix 以现代术语义出现。

items.en: The verb to suffix and the study of word formation grow from the noun.
items.cn: 动词用法与构词研究都由这个名词衍生。

note.en: Suffix is built from sub- and figere, like affix, fix, and fixture, and it stands beside prefix, infix, and suffixal in grammar.
note.cn: suffix 由 sub- 与 figere 构成，与 affix、fix、fixture 同源，语法中又与 prefix、infix、suffixal 并列。

entries.definition: a prefix or suffix added to a word
entries.definitionCN: 加在词上的前缀或后缀，同源

entries.definition: relating to a suffix
entries.definitionCN: 后缀的；与后缀有关的

entries.definition: the right to vote in elections
entries.definitionCN: 选举权；与 suffix 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a letter group added to the start of a word
entries.definitionCN: 加在词首的成分

entries.definition: an element inserted inside a word
entries.definitionCN: 插入词中的成分

entries.definition: the last part of a word, especially an inflection
entries.definitionCN: 词尾；尤指屈折成分

normalIntro.en: Suffix is a little piece fixed onto the far end of a word, and its own spelling ends in fix, the very act of fixing.
normalIntro.cn: suffix 是固定在词最末尾的一小块成分，它自己的拼写也以 fix 结尾，正是「固定」这个动作。

normal.en: Sub- means under: the piece sits under the end of the word, trailing behind the stem.
normal.cn: sub- 表示在下：小块成分挂在词尾之下，拖在词干后面。

normal.en: Fix is to make fast: a suffix is the bit made fast after the main word.
normal.cn: fix 意为固定：后缀就是固定在主词之后的那一块。

normal.en: Compare prefix: pre- means before, sub- means after or under, so the two ends are easy to tell apart.
normal.cn: 对比 prefix：pre- 表示在前，sub- 表示在后或在下面，两端一看就分得清。

normal.en: A suffix changes category: -ness turns adjectives into nouns, as in kindness.
normal.cn: 后缀改变词类：-ness 把形容词变名词，如 kindness。

normal.en: An inflectional suffix only changes form: -ed marks past tense but makes no new word.
normal.cn: 屈折后缀只改变形式：-ed 标记过去时，却不造新词。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden tag wired to the tail of a finished word.
abstract.cn: 想象一只木牌用细铁线挂在已写完的词尾巴上。

abstract.en: Watch the final -ed click on like a cap that fits only the last thread of a bolt.
abstract.cn: 看着最后的 -ed 咔嗒一下扣上，像只配得上螺栓最后一圈螺纹的螺帽。

abstract.en: Think of a train that keeps adding one little caboose at the very back.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车不断在最后面挂上一节小小的守车。

examples.en: The suffix -ful means full of, as in hopeful.
examples.cn: 后缀 -ful 表示充满，如 hopeful。

examples.en: Some learners confuse the suffix with the stem of a word.
examples.cn: 有些学习者把后缀和词干搞混。

examples.en: Adding the same suffix to two stems can give different meanings.
examples.cn: 给两个词干加上同一个后缀，可能得到不同的意思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒非克思」——撒一件小东西在词的最后面，把它固定住；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ figere（固定）→ 拉丁语 suffigere（在下面固定）→ 现代拉丁语名词 suffixum（固定在末尾之物）→ 英语 suffix，核心义「固定在词尾的成分」。

sensesIntro.en: Suffix begins as a letter group fastened to the end of a word, then covers grammatical endings, words so formed, anything tacked on at the end, and the verb of adding one.
sensesIntro.cn: suffix 先指固定在词尾的一串字母，继而指语法上的屈折词尾、由此构成的整词、任何加在末尾的东西，以及加后缀这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small tag wired to the tail of a finished word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小牌挂在已写完的词尾巴上。

branches.en: A word-forming suffix is the central, everyday sense.
branches.cn: 构词后缀是最核心、最日常的义项。

branches.en: An inflectional ending is the grammar-marking branch of the same position.
branches.cn: 屈折词尾是同一末尾位置上的语法标记分支。

branches.en: The whole word formed this way can itself be called a suffixed word.
branches.cn: 这样构成的整词也可称作带后缀的词。

branches.en: Numbers, notes, and other elements tacked on at the end share the appended sense.
branches.cn: 数字、注释等加在末尾的成分共享「附加」这一层意思。

branches.en: The verb suffixes something when it fastens an ending on.
branches.cn: 动词用法指把词尾固定上去。

intro.en: Suffix is itself a compound of a Latin prefix and a Latin root, and the field around it is a small map of affixes.
intro.cn: suffix 本身就是「拉丁前缀 + 拉丁词根」的合成词，围绕它的术语构成一幅小小的词缀地图。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- means under or near, and figere means to fasten, so affix and fix share the fixing act.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 意为在下或近旁，figere 意为固定，因此 affix 与 fix 共享相同的动作。

items.example: The prefix sub- gives suffix its underside.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 给出 suffix 底下那一层的意思。

items.example: Figere gives the fastening image.
items.exampleCN: figere 提供固定的意象。

items.meaning: an ending added to a word
items.example: Suffix names the piece at the end.
items.exampleCN: suffix 指末尾的那一块。

items.example: Affix covers both ends.
items.exampleCN: affix 涵盖两端。

items.meaning: an element added at the front
items.example: Prefix places the piece first.
items.exampleCN: prefix 把这块放在最前。

items.example: The suffix -al forms suffixed adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成带后缀的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms suffixation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 suffixation。

items.example: The suffix -al forms suffixal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 suffixal。

definition_zh: 窒息；闷死；被闷住的憋闷感；压抑窒息的状态
definition_en: the state of being unable to breathe, or the act of killing someone or something by stopping the air
core_image: 一只无形的手从外面按住口鼻，空气被挡在咽喉之外
scene: 地下车库的空气一片污浊，他感到胸口被什么东西堵住，几乎透不过气。In the underground car park the air was foul, and he felt a tightening in his chest close to suffocation.
sceneCN: 这里 suffocation 是「憋闷、快要透不过气的感觉」（第 3 个义项：被闷住的窒息感）；句意：地下车库的空气一片污浊，他感到胸口被什么东西堵住，几乎透不过气。

derivatives.zh: 由 -ate 动词去掉词尾加 -ion 得到，义为「使窒息；憋闷」
由 -ing 构成，义为「令人窒息的」
由 -ed 构成，义为「被闷住的」
由 -ly 构成，义为「令人窒息地」

senses.title: Being unable to breathe
senses.definition: the condition of being unable to get air into the lungs
senses.definitionCN: 无法把空气吸入肺部的状态
senses.example: Suffocation can follow when the airway is blocked for only a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 只要呼吸道被堵塞几分钟，就可能发生窒息。
senses.why: Latin suffocare means to choke or throttle, and the noun ending -ion turns that choking act into a named state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 suffocare 意为使窒息、掐住喉咙，名词词尾 -ion 把这个动作转成一种被命名的状态。

senses.title: Killing by cutting off air
senses.definition: the act of killing a person or animal by blocking the breathing passages
senses.definitionCN: 阻塞呼吸通道而导致人或动物死亡的行为
senses.example: The report gave suffocation as the probable cause of death.
senses.exampleCN: 报告认为死因很可能是窒息。
senses.why: The same choking image gains an outcome, so the noun also names the fatal act and its official verdict.
senses.whyCN: 同一个掐喉意象加上了结果，于是这个词也指致命的动作及其正式结论。

senses.title: The feeling of being smothered
senses.definition: an oppressive sense that the air is too close or too heavy to breathe
senses.definitionCN: 空气闷重压抑、几乎无法呼吸的感觉
senses.example: The heat in the small attic room felt like suffocation.
senses.exampleCN: 闷热的小阁楼房间让人有窒息般的憋闷感。
senses.why: The noun can name the sensation itself rather than any physical blocking, so it covers stuffy rooms and crowds.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指感觉本身，而非任何物理阻塞，因此能用于闷热的房间和拥挤的人群。

senses.title: Feeling trapped and overwhelmed
senses.definition: a figurative sense of being crushed by people, rules, or pressure that leave no room to act
senses.definitionCN: 被人群、规定或压力压得毫无行动空间的比喻性窒息感
senses.example: She described her job as suffocation, with no space for any idea.
senses.exampleCN: 她形容自己的工作让人窒息，容不下任何想法。
senses.why: When air stands for freedom, having no air becomes a picture of having no room to breathe freely in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 当空气代表自由时，没有空气就成了日常生活中无法自由喘息的一幅画面。

senses.title: Lack of air for plants or fire
senses.definition: the death or fading of plants or the smothering of a flame for want of air
senses.definitionCN: 植物因缺氧而枯萎或火焰因缺氧而熄灭
senses.example: Waterlogged soil can suffocate the roots, and smoke can do the same to a fire.
senses.exampleCN: 积水土壤会使根系窒息，浓烟也会让火焰熄灭。
senses.why: The choking image moves from lungs to roots and flames, which likewise die when the air stops.
senses.whyCN: 掐喉意象从肺部移到根与火，它们同样在空气断绝时死亡。

intro.en: Suffocation comes from Latin suffocare, to choke, through suffocatio, the noun for the choking itself.
intro.cn: suffocation 来自拉丁语 suffocare（使窒息），经由名词 suffocatio（窒息），直接进入英语。

items.en: Fauces means the throat, and suffocare is formed on the idea of closing it.
items.cn: fauces 意为喉咙，suffocare 建立在「把喉咙堵住」这一想法之上。

items.en: Suffocare means to choke, throttle, or smother.
items.cn: suffocare 意为使窒息、掐住、闷死。

items.en: Suffocatio names the choking, either as an act or as a state.
items.cn: suffocatio 指窒息，既可指动作也可指状态。

items.en: The noun is used for death by lack of air and for stifled air in enclosed spaces.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，该名词用于缺氧致死以及密闭空间的闷浊空气。

items.en: Suffocation enters English in medical texts on choking and smothering.
items.cn: suffocation 在十四世纪以医学术语进入英语，指窒息与闷死。

items.en: The figurative sense of a suffocating feeling or environment develops.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出「令人窒息的感觉或环境」这一比喻义。

note.en: Suffocation belongs to the suffoc- family with suffocate, suffocating, and suffocated, and it stands beside the plain choking and smothering words.
note.cn: suffocation 与 suffocate、suffocating、suffocated 同属 suffoc- 词族，与 choking、smothering 这类直白的窒息词并列。

entries.definition: to be unable to breathe or stop something breathing
entries.definitionCN: 使窒息；无法呼吸

entries.definition: making it hard to breathe
entries.definitionCN: 令人窒息的

entries.definition: tending to choke or smother
entries.definitionCN: 有窒息倾向的，罕见同源形容词

entries.definition: a severe lack of oxygen marked by loss of consciousness
entries.definitionCN: 严重缺氧导致昏迷的医学概念

entries.definition: the act of being unable to breathe because of a blockage
entries.definitionCN: 因堵塞而无法呼吸

entries.definition: covering the mouth and nose so that breathing stops
entries.definitionCN: 捂住口鼻使人无法呼吸

normalIntro.en: Suffocation is the choking act of suffocare turned into a named state by the noun ending -ion, so breath and blockage sit in one word.
normalIntro.cn: suffocation 是 suffocare 的掐喉动作被名词词尾 -ion 转成一种状态，因此呼吸与堵塞同在一词之中。

normal.en: Latin fauces means throat: suffoc- carries the throat image, so the word points straight at the pipe that carries air.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 fauces 意为喉咙：suffoc- 带着喉咙的意象，这个词直指输送空气的管道。

normal.en: The ending -ion marks an abstract noun, just as in action and protection.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ion 标记抽象名词，正如 action 与 protection。

normal.en: The base verb suffocate keeps the act, while suffocation names the act or state.
normal.cn: 动词 suffocate 保留动作，suffocation 则指动作或状态。

normal.en: The adjective suffocating describes air, rooms, or heat that make breathing hard.
normal.cn: 形容词 suffocating 描述令人呼吸困难的空气、房间或热气。

normal.en: Compare asphyxia: asphyxia is a medical term for oxygen shortage, suffocation is the everyday state.
normal.cn: 对比 asphyxia：它是缺氧的医学术语，suffocation 则是日常所说的窒息状态。

abstract.en: Picture a hand clamped over nose and mouth from the outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从外面捂住口鼻。

abstract.en: Think of a pillow pressed down and the last pocket of air shrinking away.
abstract.cn: 想象枕头压下去，最后一点空气被挤走。

abstract.en: Feel a small stuffy room with the window painted shut.
abstract.cn: 感受一间窗户被钉死的闷热小屋。

examples.en: The plastic bag carried a warning about the risk of suffocation.
examples.cn: 塑料袋上印有窒息风险的警示。

examples.en: Firefighters wear masks to protect them from suffocation in thick smoke.
examples.cn: 消防员戴面具以防在浓烟中窒息。

examples.en: She felt a mild suffocation in the crowded lift.
examples.cn: 在拥挤的电梯里她感到一阵轻微的窒闷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒佛开身」——仿佛佛像都张开手掌让人透口气，可这里偏偏是气被堵住；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fauces（喉咙）→ 拉丁语 suffocare（掐住喉咙、使窒息）→ 拉丁语 suffocatio（窒息）→ 英语 suffocation，核心义「喉咙被堵住、气进不来」。

sensesIntro.en: Suffocation starts from the stuffy feeling of choking, then covers physical choking, emotional smothering, and death by lack of air.
sensesIntro.cn: suffocation 从憋闷的感觉起步，先后指真实的窒息与情感上的压抑，最终指因缺氧而致死的致命窒息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible hand pressing down on nose and mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只无形的手从外面按住口鼻。

branches.en: The plain physical inability to breathe is the first sense.
branches.cn: 身体上无法呼吸是第一个义项。

branches.en: The fatal act and its official verdict branch off from the same choke.
branches.cn: 致命动作与其正式结论从同一个「掐喉」分出。

branches.en: The felt sensation and the trapped feeling are inward branches, one bodily and one social.
branches.cn: 身体感受与被困感是向内延伸的两支，一为身体，一为社会关系。

branches.en: Plants and flames also die when air stops, so the image widens beyond lungs.
branches.cn: 植物与火焰在空气断绝时同样死去，意象因而越出肺部。

branches.en: A stuffy room and a real blockage share the same shrinking of available air.
branches.cn: 闷热的房间与真实的堵塞共享同一种空气变少的体验。

intro.en: Suffocation sits at the centre of a Latin family: suffocate, suffocating, suffocated, and the medical term asphyxia all point to the throat.
intro.cn: suffocation 位于一个拉丁词族的中心：suffocate、suffocating、suffocated 以及医学词 asphyxia 都指向喉咙。

latinIntro.en: Latin fauces means throat and suffocare means to choke, so the -foc- stem of suffocation holds the narrow passage of breath.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fauces 意为喉咙，suffocare 意为使窒息，因此 suffocation 的 -foc- 词干藏着呼吸的窄通道。

items.example: Suffocare supplies the choking image.
items.exampleCN: suffocare 提供掐喉的意象。

items.example: Fauces points at the narrow passage.
items.exampleCN: fauces 指向狭窄的通道。

items.example: Suffocatio is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: suffocatio 是直接来源。

items.example: Suffocate is the everyday verb.
items.exampleCN: suffocate 是日常动词。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms suffocation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 suffocation。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms suffocating air.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成感到窒息的空气。

items.example: The suffix -ated forms suffocated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ated 构成 suffocated。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms suffocatingly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 suffocatingly。

items.meaning: loss of pulse from lack of oxygen
items.example: Asphyxia is the medical cousin of suffocation.
items.exampleCN: asphyxia 是 suffocation 的医学近亲。

definition_zh: （光、色、液体）充满；弥漫；（情绪）充满；使布满
definition_en: to spread over or fill something, especially a surface, with light, color, liquid, or feeling
core_image: 颜色像水一样从底下慢慢渗上来，把整个人或整片区域染满
scene: 夕阳西下，整片山谷被金红色的光慢慢染透。As the sun went down, a warm golden light began to suffuse the whole valley.
sceneCN: 这里 suffuse 是「（光、色）弥漫、充满」（第 1 个义项：光或颜色充斥某处）；句意：夕阳西下，整片山谷被金红色的光慢慢染透。

pos.zh: 使充满；使弥漫；（液体、光、色）布满

derivatives.zh: 由 -ion 构成，义为「弥漫；泛红」
由 -ive 构成，义为「弥漫的；扩散的」，较少见
由 -ed 构成，义为「布满的；弥漫着……的」

senses.title: To spread light or colour over
senses.definition: to spread gradually over a place, surface, or object so that it is filled with light or colour
senses.definitionCN: 光或颜色逐渐铺满某处、某表面或某物，使其被填满
senses.example: Dawn began to suffuse the eastern sky with pink.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明的粉色开始弥漫东边的天空。
senses.why: Latin suffundere means to pour below, and light and colour seem to rise from underneath a surface until it glows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 suffundere 意为在下面倾倒，而光与色仿佛是自表面之下涌上来，直到通体发亮。

senses.title: To fill with liquid or moisture
senses.definition: to flood or permeate a surface or body with liquid, tears, or blood
senses.definitionCN: 让液体、泪水或血液漫遍某个表面或身体
senses.example: Tears suffused her eyes when she heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到消息时，泪水盈满了她的眼眶。
senses.why: The pouring image is most literal here: moisture gathers below the surface and rises until it covers what it touches.
senses.whyCN: 这是「在下面倾倒」最字面的一层：水分聚在表面之下，一直涨上来，直到浸满所及之处。

senses.title: To be filled with feeling
senses.definition: to fill a person, a room, or a face with a strong emotion such as joy, warmth, or sadness
senses.definitionCN: 让喜悦、温暖或悲伤等强烈情感充满一个人、一间屋子或一张脸
senses.example: A deep sense of calm suffused the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 一种深沉的平静弥漫了整个房间。
senses.why: Feelings behave like liquid: they gather below the surface and rise, so joy or calm can pour through a person or a room.
senses.whyCN: 情感像液体那样，聚在表面之下再涌上来，所以喜悦与平静会像水一样灌满一个人或一间屋子。

senses.title: To tinge a tissue with colour
senses.definition: to flush or stain a body part or tissue with blood in a medical description
senses.definitionCN: 在医学描述中以血液为某部位或组织染色泛红
senses.example: The inflamed joint was suffused with blood.
senses.exampleCN: 发炎的关节处充血泛红。
senses.why: Medical use keeps the liquid image but fixes its colour to blood, so the verb describes tissue turning red from within.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法保留液体意象，但把颜色固定为血，于是动词描述组织由内而外泛红。

senses.title: To add something throughout
senses.definition: to spread a quality, tone, or mood through something such as a text, a voice, or a piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 把某种品质、语调或情绪散布在文本、嗓音或乐曲之中
senses.example: Sorrow suffuses every line of the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 哀伤浸润了这封信的每一行。
senses.why: Once a feeling or quality is imagined as something poured in, it can run through any whole, including words and notes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把情感或品质想象成倾倒进去的东西，它便能贯穿任何整体，包括文字与音符。

intro.en: Suffuse comes from Latin suffundere, to pour underneath, made of sub, under, and fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: suffuse 来自拉丁语 suffundere（在下面倾倒），由 sub（在下）与 fundere（倾倒）构成。

items.en: Fundere means to pour out, especially a liquid.
items.cn: fundere 意为倾出，尤指液体。

items.en: Sub means under, and suffundere means to pour below or pour over something.
items.cn: sub 意为在下，suffundere 意为向下倾倒或浇在某物之上。

items.en: The past participle suffusus is used for colour and liquid spreading over a surface.
items.cn: 中古拉丁语中，过去分词 suffusus 用于描述颜色或液体铺满表面。

items.en: Suffusare, a reworked form built on suffusus, carries the same spreading sense.
items.cn: 以 suffusus 重造的拉丁词形 suffusare 同样带有弥漫之意。

items.en: English suffuse is formed from suffusus and first describes liquid and colour spreading.
items.cn: 英语 suffuse 由 suffusus 构成，最初描述液体与颜色的铺展。

items.en: The verb extends to feeling and mood, as in a room suffused with warmth.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词延伸到情感与气氛，如 a room suffused with warmth。

note.en: Suffuse belongs to the Latin pour family with effuse, transfuse, and profuse, and it stands beside spread, pervade, and permeate in meaning.
note.cn: suffuse 与 effuse、transfuse、profuse 同属拉丁「倾倒」词族，在意义上与 spread、pervade、permeate 相邻。

entries.definition: to transfer blood or a liquid into a body
entries.definitionCN: 输（血）；灌输

entries.definition: to pour out freely, or to spread out
entries.definitionCN: 溢出；流出

entries.definition: to spread widely in all directions
entries.definitionCN: 扩散；散布

entries.definition: to spread through every part of
entries.definitionCN: 遍布；弥漫于

entries.definition: to pass or spread through something
entries.definitionCN: 渗透；透过

entries.definition: to fill with a strong feeling or quality
entries.definitionCN: 灌输；使充满

normalIntro.en: Suffuse is Latin sub plus fundere, so the whole word is a pouring from below that rises until the surface is entirely covered.
normalIntro.cn: suffuse 是拉丁语 sub 加 fundere，整词就是在下面倾倒，一直漫上来直到表面全被盖住。

normal.en: Fuse looks like the pouring root but means melt, so keep suffuse apart from fusion.
normal.cn: fuse 看似倒出词根，其实意为熔化，要把 suffuse 与 fusion 分开。

normal.en: Suffuse usually takes with: a room is suffused with light.
normal.cn: suffuse 常用 with：房间被光充满。

normal.en: The past participle suffused works as an adjective, as in a face suffused with joy.
normal.cn: 过去分词 suffused 可作形容词，如喜气洋洋的脸。

normal.en: The noun suffusion names the spreading, as of colour in the cheeks.
normal.cn: 名词 suffusion 指弥漫扩散，如脸颊泛红。

normal.en: Compare transfuse with trans-: there the liquid moves from one body into another, here it spreads over.
normal.cn: 对比带 trans- 的 transfuse：那里液体从一体移入另一体，这里只是铺满。

abstract.en: Picture colour seeping up through a sheet of paper until the whole page glows.
abstract.cn: 想象颜色从纸的背面渗上来，直到整页发亮。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp placed beneath a thin curtain, its glow swelling until the cloth is full of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯放在薄帘子底下，光晕胀开，直到整块布都盛满了光。

abstract.en: Feel a warm wave of feeling rise from the chest and spread over the face.
abstract.cn: 感觉一阵暖流从胸口涌起，铺满整张脸。

examples.en: A pale blue light suffused the early morning mist.
examples.cn: 淡蓝色的光弥漫在清晨的薄雾中。

examples.en: Her cheeks were suffused with embarrassment after the mistake.
examples.cn: 出了差错后，她的双颊因窘迫而泛红。

examples.en: The garden was suffused with the scent of jasmine by evening.
examples.cn: 到傍晚时，花园里弥漫着茉莉的香气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「洒服斯」——仿佛把颜色洒下来，服服帖帖地铺满整个平面；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ fundere（倾倒）→ 拉丁语 suffundere（在下面倾倒）→ 过去分词 suffusus → 英国造词 suffuse，核心义「从下面漫上来、把表面铺满」。

sensesIntro.en: Suffuse begins from something poured beneath a surface, then spreads to light, water, blood, feeling, and mood.
sensesIntro.cn: suffuse 先是光与颜色从表面之下漫上来，继而用于液体、情感、组织中渗血，最后用于某种特质贯穿整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: colour rising from below and soaking a whole surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：颜色从下面漫上来，浸透整个表面。

branches.en: Light and colour filling a place is the visual, most common sense.
branches.cn: 光与色充满某处是最常见、最可视的义项。

branches.en: Liquid pouring until it covers is the literal branch of the same image.
branches.cn: 液体漫上来覆盖表面是同一意象最字面的一支。

branches.en: Emotion and quality behave like a poured-in substance, filling people and running through works.
branches.cn: 情感与品质像被倒进来的物质，既充满人也贯穿作品。

branches.en: Medical use fixes the liquid to blood and the surface to tissue.
branches.cn: 医学用法把液体定为血，把表面定为组织。

branches.en: Both a lit room and a joyous face look filled from within.
branches.cn: 被照亮的房间与喜悦的脸都是从内部被填满的样子。

intro.en: Suffuse shares the Latin root fundere with transfuse and effuse, and the suffix -ion builds its noun suffusion.
intro.cn: suffuse 与 transfuse、effuse 共享拉丁词根 fundere，词尾 -ion 构成名词 suffusion。

latinIntro.en: Latin fundere means to pour, and the prefix sub adds direction from below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fundere 意为倾倒，前缀 sub 加上了「自下而上」的方向。

items.example: The prefix sub- points the pouring upward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把倾倒指向从下往上的方向。

items.example: Fundere gives the pouring image.
items.exampleCN: fundere 提供倾倒的意象。

items.example: Suffundere joins both halves.
items.exampleCN: suffundere 把两半合成一体。

items.example: Suffusus is the participle behind the verb.
items.exampleCN: suffusus 是它背后的分词形式。

items.example: Suffuse keeps the Latin pouring sense.
items.exampleCN: suffuse 保留了拉丁语倾倒之意。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms suffusion.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 suffusion。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms suffusive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 suffusive。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms suffused.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 suffused。

items.meaning: to pour across into another body
items.example: Transfuse swaps sub- for trans-.
items.exampleCN: transfuse 把 sub- 换成了 trans-。

definition_zh: 想自杀的；有自杀倾向的；自我毁灭的；极度危险的
definition_en: wanting to kill yourself, or describing a plan, act or situation that is very likely to destroy someone or something
core_image: 一个人独自站在高楼天台的边缘，脚下是深渊
scene: 深夜的急救电话突然响起，接线员一边安抚一边联系家属。The counsellor said that the caller sounded intensely suicidal.
sceneCN: 这里 suicidal 是「有自杀意图的」（第 1 个义项：表现出想结束自己生命倾向的）；句意为咨询师说，来电者听起来有强烈的自杀倾向。画面中可辨认的物件：电话、值班记录本、窗外夜色。

pos.zh: 有自杀倾向的；想自杀的
极度危险的；极可能失败的

collocations.zh: 有自杀倾向；觉得生无可恋

derivatives.zh: 名词基础词，义为「自杀」
形容词加 -ly，义为「以自毁的方式」
形容词加 -ity，医学上指「自杀风险」
形容词加 -ness，义为「自杀倾向性」

senses.title: Wanting to end your own life
senses.titleCN: 想自杀的；有自杀倾向的
senses.definition: having thoughts of or a strong wish to kill yourself
senses.definitionCN: 有结束自己生命的念头或强烈愿望
senses.example: After weeks without sleep she began to feel suicidal.
senses.exampleCN: 连续几周失眠之后，她开始产生自杀的念头。
senses.why: The adjective is built on suicide, so it first names a state of mind pointing toward self-destruction.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接由名词 suicide 加词尾构成，所以最初就指向「心里想要自我毁灭」的状态。

senses.title: Likely to harm yourself
senses.titleCN: 有自伤行为的；带自杀倾向的
senses.definition: describing a gesture, attempt or cry for help that may lead to serious self-harm
senses.definitionCN: 形容可能导致严重自伤的姿态、尝试或求救信号
senses.example: The school referred the pupil for a suicidal gesture.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把那名学生的自伤行为转介去做了评估。
senses.why: When the wish leaks out into visible action, the word moves from feeling to behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 当内心的念头外化为可见的行为时，这个词就从情绪层面走到了行为层面。

senses.title: Self-destructing a plan or decision
senses.definition: describing an action or plan that is certain to ruin the person, group or cause behind it
senses.definitionCN: 形容必然毁掉当事人、团体或目标的行动或计划
senses.example: Walking into that debate unprepared would be suicidal.
senses.exampleCN: 毫无准备就走进那场辩论，无异于自我毁灭。
senses.why: The original image spreads to anything that destroys itself by its own motion, so a reckless plan gets the label.
senses.whyCN: 原本的画面延伸到了任何因自身动作而毁灭的事物，于是一个莽撞的计划也会被这样称呼。

senses.title: Extremely risky for a business or team
senses.definition: used of a policy or price war that could destroy a company, team or market position
senses.definitionCN: 形容可能毁掉公司、球队或市场地位的政策或价格战
senses.example: Cutting prices that low would be commercially suicidal.
senses.exampleCN: 把价格压到那么低，在商业上极为危险。
senses.why: Commercial use keeps the literal danger but moves it from a body to an organisation.
senses.whyCN: 商业用法保留了字面上的危险感，只是把承受者从身体换成了组织。

senses.title: Heading towards collapse
senses.titleCN: 注定失败的；走向崩溃的
senses.definition: describing a course of action or a process that is clearly doomed to fail
senses.definitionCN: 形容明显注定失败的行动路线或进程
senses.example: Ignoring the warning signs is a suicidal way to run a project.
senses.exampleCN: 无视警示信号，是一种注定失败的项目管理方式。
senses.why: The strongest step away from the body, the word now simply means certain collapse.
senses.whyCN: 这是离身体最远的一步，词义已经简化为「必然崩溃」。

senses.title: Resembling suicide in effect
senses.definition: used informally for something so rapid or fierce that it seems to destroy itself
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容某事迅猛或猛烈到仿佛在自我毁灭
senses.example: A suicidal pace in the first mile cost her the race.
senses.exampleCN: 开头第一英里就冲得太猛，她因此输掉了比赛。
senses.why: Speed that runs straight to collapse borrows the same picture, hence the sporting idiom.
senses.whyCN: 这种一路冲向崩溃的迅猛借用了同一幅画面，于是有了体育口语里的说法。

senses.title: The related adverb
senses.definition: in a manner that shows a wish to end life or that ruins oneself
senses.definitionCN: 表现出想结束生命的倾向，或做出自我毁灭的方式
senses.example: He drove suicidally fast along the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 他在山路上开得飞快，完全是拿命冒险。
senses.why: The -ly word extends the adjective to the way an act is done, with the same self-destruction image.
senses.whyCN: 副词形式把形容词延伸到「做事的姿态」上，保留着同一幅自我毁灭的画面。

intro.en: Suicidal comes from suicide, a word built in the seventeenth century from the Latin roots sui and caedere.
intro.cn: suicidal 来自 suicide；suicide 一词造于十世纪后的近代早期英语（一般认为约十七世纪中叶），由拉丁词根 sui 与 caedere 合成。

items.en: Sui is the genitive of se, meaning of oneself.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sui 是反身代词 se 的属格，意为「自己的」。

items.en: Caedere means to cut or to kill.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caedere 意为切割、杀。

items.en: Writers coin suicide to name the killing of oneself, with a native -cide ending borrowed from homicide.
items.cn: 一般认为在十七世纪三十年代的早期现代英语中，文人仿照 homicide 的 -cide 词尾造出 suicide，用来指「杀死自己」。

items.en: The sense extends to figurative self-destruction in politics, business and sport.
items.cn: 到了十九世纪，词义扩展到政治、商业与体育中比喻性的「自我毁灭」。

items.en: The adjective suicidal is formed with the -al ending and is widely used in medicine and public health.
items.cn: 形容词 suicidal 由 -al 词尾构成，在医学与公共卫生语境中广为使用。

items.en: Today suicidal also describes reckless behaviour toward oneself or an organisation.
items.cn: 今天 suicidal 还可以形容对个人或组织而言极不明智、近乎自毁的行为。

note.en: Suicidal belongs to the suicide family, and it sits near words for self-harm, danger and reckless decisions.
note.cn: suicidal 属于「自杀」这一词族，同时与表示自伤、风险与鲁莽决定的词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of killing yourself
entries.definitionCN: 自杀；自杀行为

entries.definition: in a self-destructive way
entries.definitionCN: 以自毁的方式

entries.definition: having a wish to kill another person
entries.definitionCN: 想杀人的；有杀人倾向的

entries.definition: harming your own interests or health
entries.definitionCN: 自我毁灭的；自毁的

entries.definition: acting without care for danger
entries.definitionCN: 鲁莽的；不顾后果的

entries.definition: feeling that nothing good can happen
entries.definitionCN: 绝望的；没有希望的

normalIntro.en: Suicidal is the suicide noun turned into an adjective with -al, and its sense grows from killing oneself to destroying oneself in other ways.
normalIntro.cn: suicidal 是名词 suicide 加 -al 变成的形容词，词义从「杀害自己」一路长成「以各种方式毁掉自己」。

normal.en: Sui- in Latin means of oneself, so suicide is the act of killing oneself.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 sui 意为「自己的」，所以 suicide 就是杀死自己。

normal.en: The -cide ending also appears in homicide and pesticide, meaning killing.
normal.cn: 词尾 -cide 也出现在 homicide、pesticide 中，都表示「杀」。

normal.en: Suicidal thoughts is the most common collocation, often used in medical and school contexts.
normal.cn: 「suicidal thoughts」是最常见的搭配，多用于医疗与学校语境。

normal.en: Adding -al to a noun makes an adjective, so suicide gives suicidal.
normal.cn: 名词后加 -al 构成形容词，suicide 就变成 suicidal。

normal.en: The -ly form is suicidally, as in suicidally fast, but the base form stays suicidal.
normal.cn: 副词形式是 suicidally，例如「suicidally fast」；基础形式仍是 suicidal。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked with the word exit, and a lonely figure facing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇写着「出口」的门，以及一个独自面对它的身影。

abstract.en: See a person holding a ladder over a cliff for themselves.
abstract.cn: 想象有人亲手把梯子架向悬崖。

abstract.en: Imagine a company setting its own warehouse on fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一家公司亲手点燃自己的仓库。

examples.en: Doctors screen new patients for suicidal thoughts.
examples.cn: 医生会对新病人进行自杀念头筛查。

examples.en: Raising prices during a recession would be suicide for the brand.
examples.cn: 在衰退期涨价对品牌而言无异于自毁。

examples.en: She was teased during the session for acting suicidally in practice.
examples.cn: 练习时她那种不管不顾的打法被同组人打趣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sui（碎）」加「cidal（心里）」——一个人觉得心都碎了，就想毁掉自己；这只是拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sui（自己的，反身代词 se 的属格）+ caedere（切、杀）→ 一般认为十七世纪早期现代英语仿 homicide 造出 suicide → 直译「杀自己」→ 比喻义「自我毁灭」。

sensesIntro.en: Suicidal starts with the wish to end your own life, passes through visible self-harm, and then spreads to plans, companies and speed that destroy themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: suicidal 先指想结束自己生命的念头，再指外露的自伤行为，然后扩展到会自我毁灭的计划、公司乃至速度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing alone at the edge of a high roof.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人独自站在高楼边缘。

branches.en: The medical sense names the inner wish to end life.
branches.cn: 医学义项指内心想结束生命的愿望。

branches.en: The behavioural sense names gestures that turn the wish into action.
branches.cn: 行为义项指把愿望变成动作的姿态。

branches.en: Figurative self-destruction is the picture moved from a body to a plan.
branches.cn: 比喻性的自我毁灭是把画面从身体移到了计划上。

branches.en: Business and general use keep the same danger for a company or a project.
branches.cn: 商业与一般用法把同样的危险放在公司或项目上。

branches.en: The sporting idiom and the adverb both describe going too fast toward collapse.
branches.cn: 体育习语与副词形式都在描述冲向崩溃的速度。

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin root sui, the killing element cide, and the English adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁词根 sui、表示「杀」的成分 cide，以及英语形容词词尾 -al 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sui means of oneself and caedere means to cut or kill, and the compound was modelled on homicide.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sui 意为「自己的」，caedere 意为切、杀，这个合成词是仿照 homicide 造的。

items.example: Sui is the genitive of the reflexive pronoun se.
items.exampleCN: sui 是反身代词 se 的属格形式。

items.example: Suicide was coined in early modern English.
items.exampleCN: suicide 一词造于早期现代英语。

items.example: The suffix -al forms suicidal from suicide.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把 suicide 变成 suicidal。

items.example: Suicidal keeps the self-killing image.
items.exampleCN: suicidal 保留了「杀自己」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms suicidally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 suicidally。

items.example: Clinicians assess suicidality at intake.
items.exampleCN: 临床医生在接诊时评估自杀倾向。

items.example: Homicide shares the killing element.
items.exampleCN: homicide 共享「杀」这一成分。

items.example: Caedere supplies the killing element of -cide.
items.exampleCN: caedere 提供了 -cide 中的「杀」义。

items.example: The suffix -cide appears in pesticide and homicide.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cide 出现在 pesticide 与 homicide 中。

items.example: Self-destructive overlaps the figurative sense.
items.exampleCN: self-destructive 与比喻义相互重叠。

definition_zh: 总结；概括；归纳；简而言之
definition_en: to give the main points of something in a short form, leaving out the details
core_image: 把一大摞文件压成一张写满要点的卡片
scene: 论文交稿前的最后一晚，桌上摊着厚厚的调研报告和一张便签。She summarised a forty-page report on a single page for the board.
sceneCN: 这里 summarise 是「总结、概括」（第 1 个义项：用简短的话说出要点）；句意为她为董事会把一份四十页的报告浓缩成了一页。画面中可辨认的物件：报告、便签、荧光笔。

derivatives.zh: 名词基础词，由拉丁语 summarium 缩略而来，义为「摘要」
动词加 -ation，义为「总结过程」
动词加 -er，义为「做总结的人或工具」
过去分词作定语，义为「已概括的」
美式拼写，与 summarise 同义

senses.title: To state the main points briefly
senses.definition: to say or write the most important ideas of a text, talk or event in a short form
senses.definitionCN: 用简短的话说出或写出文章、讲话或事件中最重要的意思
senses.example: In one paragraph she summarised the whole article.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一段话概括了整篇文章。
senses.why: The Latin root means the sum or the whole, so to summarise is to gather the parts into their total.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「总数、整体」，所以总结就是把各部分汇总成一个总数。

senses.title: To restate findings or results
senses.definition: to report the outcome of research, a discussion or a meeting point by point
senses.definitionCN: 逐点报告研究、讨论或会议的结果
senses.example: The chair summarised the findings before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 主席在表决前概括了调查结果。
senses.why: Research language uses the word for compressing conclusions, where the detail sits in tables and the summary sits in words.
senses.whyCN: 科研语境用它来压缩结论，细节留在表格里，文字里只放摘要。

senses.title: To give an outline without detail
senses.definition: to describe the general line of a story, argument or plan without detail
senses.definitionCN: 不带细节地描述故事、论点或计划的大致脉络
senses.example: He summarised the plot in three sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 他用三句话简述了情节。
senses.why: Because the root counts totals, the word fits anything that can be cut down to an outline.
senses.whyCN: 因为词根与「总数」有关，凡是能压缩成大纲的东西都适用这个词。

senses.title: To shorten a document in writing
senses.definition: to make a written abstract or condensed version of a longer document
senses.definitionCN: 为较长的文件撰写书面摘要或压缩版本
senses.example: Please summarise the contract in plain English.
senses.exampleCN: 请用通俗的英语把这份合同概括一下。
senses.why: The act becomes a written artefact when the summary itself is the product.
senses.whyCN: 当摘要本身成为产物时，这个动作就从口头表述变成了写出来的文本。

senses.title: To open or close with a recap
senses.definition: to use a short recap to open or close a talk, meeting or essay
senses.definitionCN: 在报告、会议或文章的开头或结尾用简短回顾收束
senses.example: The lecturer summarised the previous session before beginning.
senses.exampleCN: 讲师开始前先回顾了上一讲的内容。
senses.why: This use grows from the structural role of a summary as a hinge between parts.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法源自摘要作为各部分之间枢纽的结构作用。

senses.title: To give a quick account
senses.definition: to tell someone what happened in a few words, especially quickly
senses.definitionCN: 用几句话、尤其快速地告诉别人发生了什么
senses.example: Could you summarise what the doctor said?
senses.exampleCN: 你能简单说说医生讲了什么吗？
senses.why: In conversation the word softens a request for information into a quick account.
senses.whyCN: 在对话中，这个词把索取信息变成了一次简短的转述。

senses.title: The summary that is a thing
senses.definition: a short statement that gives the main points of something
senses.definitionCN: 给出某事要点的简短陈述
senses.example: The executive summary ends with five recommendations.
senses.exampleCN: 这份执行摘要以五条建议收尾。
senses.why: The noun is the recorded result of the verb, and learners must keep the two apart.
senses.whyCN: 名词是动词的成果记录，学习者要把两者区分清楚。

intro.en: Summarise is built on summary, which comes from the Latin summarium, a short statement made from a summa, a total.
intro.cn: summarise 由 summary 派生；summary 来自拉丁语 summarium（从 summa「总数」得来的简短陈述）。

items.en: Summa means the top or the total of a set of numbers.
items.cn: 拉丁语 summa 意为顶端，也指一组数字的总数。

items.en: Summarium adds a noun ending to summa, giving a statement that states the whole.
items.cn: summarium 在 summa 后加名词词尾，指「陈述整体的简要说明」。

items.en: Sommaire passes the word into French and on toward English.
items.cn: sommaire 把这个词带进法语，并继续传向英语。

items.en: Summary names a brief statement of the main points in English.
items.cn: 英语中 summary 指要点简短的陈述。

items.en: The verb summarise is formed from summary with the -ise ending.
items.cn: 动词 summarise 由 summary 加 -ise 词尾构成，一般认为首见于十九世纪。

items.en: American English writes summarize with -ize, and both forms are standard in IELTS writing.
items.cn: 美式英语写作 summarize 用 -ize；在雅思写作中两种拼写都被视为标准。

note.en: Summarise sits in the family of summary, sum, abstract and outline, and its near meanings are all about shortening.
note.cn: summarise 与 summary、sum、abstract、outline 同属一族，近义词都与「压缩、缩短」有关。

normal.en: In essays, to summarise is often used to close a paragraph before a conclusion.

normal.cn: 过去分词是 summarised，用于已经压缩好的文件。

definition_zh: 总结；综述；求和；叠加；结案陈词
definition_en: the act of adding things together or of giving the total and main points of something
core_image: 一列数字被加到最下面，得到一个总和
scene: 法庭里，双方律师都已陈述完毕，法官示意最后发言。The lawyer began her summation with a single date.
sceneCN: 这里 summation 是「结案陈词、总结性陈述」（第 2 个义项：把要点汇总后作的全篇陈述）；句意为律师以一个日期作为结案陈词的开头。画面中可辨认的物件：木质法台、卷宗、法官的槌。

derivatives.zh: 加 -e 构成动词，义为「加总、求和」
加 -ive，义为「总结性的（如总结性评估）」
同根名词，义为「总数、金额」
同根名词，义为「摘要、总结」

senses.title: The act of gathering a total
senses.definition: the act or result of adding numbers or facts together into a single total
senses.definitionCN: 把数字或事实相加成一个总数的行为或结果
senses.example: The summation of the monthly figures gave the yearly total.
senses.exampleCN: 把每月数字汇总起来，就得出了全年的总数。
senses.why: The Latin root summa is a total, and -tion names the act of reaching that total.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 summa 是总数，-tion 表示「达成这个总数的动作」。

senses.title: A summary statement of evidence
senses.definition: a speech or passage that gathers the main points, especially at the end of a trial or debate
senses.definitionCN: 把要点汇聚起来的讲话或段落，尤指审判或辩论结束时的陈述
senses.example: In her summation the lawyer named three key points.
senses.exampleCN: 律师在结案陈词中列出了三个关键点。
senses.why: Adding facts into a total becomes adding arguments into one closing speech.
senses.whyCN: 把事实加成总数，就变成了把论点汇成一段收尾的讲话。

senses.title: A general account written down
senses.definition: a written or spoken account that brings many details together into one statement
senses.definitionCN: 把许多细节汇聚成一段陈述的书面或口头论述
senses.example: His book is a summation of forty years of research.
senses.exampleCN: 他的书是对四十年研究的综述。
senses.why: When the whole is written down, the total becomes a body of knowledge in one place.
senses.whyCN: 当总量被写下来，这个「总数」就变成了一处集中的知识。

senses.title: The nerve adding its signals
senses.definition: the combined effect of several stimuli or nerve signals firing close together
senses.definitionCN: 若干刺激或神经信号在相近时间发放所产生的叠加效应
senses.example: Repetitive stimulation causes summation at the synapse.
senses.exampleCN: 重复刺激会在突触处产生总和效应。
senses.why: The arithmetical image of adding transfers directly to physiology, where signals add up until a threshold is crossed.
senses.whyCN: 算术意义上的「相加」直接搬到生理学：信号累加，直到越过阈值。

senses.title: Adding forces or effects
senses.definition: the process in which two or more forces, waves or effects combine into one resultant
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个力、波或效应合成为一个合量的过程
senses.example: The summation of the two forces produced a diagonal movement.
senses.exampleCN: 两个力的合成产生了对角线方向上的运动。
senses.why: Physics reuses the counting sense for vectors, where adding is done by geometry.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把「相加」的计数义用于矢量，只是加法改由几何来完成。

senses.title: The closing words of an argument
senses.definition: the final part of an essay or argument that restates its main claim
senses.definitionCN: 文章或论证中重述主要观点的结尾部分
senses.example: The essay ends with a brief summation of its claim.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章以对所持观点的简短总结收尾。
senses.why: The structural close grows from the courtroom summation, now applied to writing.
senses.whyCN: 这种结构性收尾源自法庭上的结案陈词，如今用到了写作中。

senses.title: The summarised result itself
senses.definition: the outcome collected in one place, as a list or set of figures
senses.definitionCN: 集中在一处的成果，如清单或一组数字
senses.example: The spreadsheet holds the summation of every invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 这张表格存放着每张发票的汇总结果。
senses.why: Because -tion can name either the act or its product, the summation can also be the thing you get.
senses.whyCN: -tion 既可指动作也可指产物，所以 summation 也可以是最终得到的那份东西。

intro.en: Summation comes from Latin summa, the total or highest point, by way of the verb summare and the -tion ending.
intro.cn: summation 来自拉丁语 summa（总数、最高点），经由动词 summare 与 -tion 词尾构成。

items.en: Summa is the top of something and also the total of a set.
items.cn: 拉丁语 summa 指某物的顶端，也指一组事物的总数。

items.en: Medieval Latin makes summare, to add up, and summatio, a reckoning.
items.cn: 中古拉丁语造出 summare（相加）与 summatio（结算），一般认为是行文用词。

items.en: Summation enters English meaning an adding up or a total.
items.cn: summation 进入英语时指相加或总数，一般认为首见于十五世纪。

items.en: Law uses summation for the closing speech that adds up the evidence.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，法律语境用 summation 指汇总证据的结案陈词。

items.en: Physiology and physics borrow the word for added nerve signals and combined forces.
items.cn: 二十世纪的生理学与物理学借用该词，表示神经信号的累加与力的合成。

items.en: Today summation works for totals, closing statements and the result of summarising.
items.cn: 今天 summation 可用于总数、结尾陈述以及概括后的成果。

note.en: Summation belongs to the sum family and shares a field with summary, total and the trial speech.
note.cn: summation 属于 sum 词族，与 summary、total 以及法庭陈述处于同一义场。
